explanation: Rule 49(2) requires the arbitration method in the contract to be consistent with Pakistani law.

question: Under Rule 50, any unauthorized breach of the Public Procurement Rules amounts to:
options: A criminal offence under the Ordinance automatically
correctAnswer: Mis-procurement
explanation: Rule 50 defines any unauthorized breach of these rules as mis-procurement.

question: Under Rule 51 (Overriding effect), these rules have effect:
options: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other rules concerning public procurements
Only for procurements above Rs. 10 million
Only where no other rule conflicts
Subject to provincial rules taking precedence
correctAnswer: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other rules concerning public procurements
explanation: Rule 51 gives the Public Procurement Rules, 2004 an overriding effect over any contrary procurement rules.

question: Under the proviso to Rule 51, prevailing (earlier) rules and procedures remain applicable only for procurements:
options: Completed before 2004 with no ongoing dispute
For which the notice for invitation of bids had been issued prior to commencement of these rules, unless the agency deems it appropriate to re-issue the notice
correctAnswer: For which the notice for invitation of bids had been issued prior to commencement of these rules, unless the agency deems it appropriate to re-issue the notice
explanation: The proviso to Rule 51 grandfathers procurements where the bid invitation notice predates these rules, unless the agency chooses to reissue the notice.

question: What is the status of Rule 52 in the current version of the Public Procurement Rules, 2004?
options: It remains fully in force, dealing with penalties
It shall be omitted (per S.R.O. No. 442(I)/2020 dated 15th May, 2020)
It deals exclusively with Schedule-I commodities
correctAnswer: It shall be omitted (per S.R.O. No. 442(I)/2020 dated 15th May, 2020)
explanation: A footnote confirms 'Rule 52. Shall be omitted' vide S.R.O. No. 442(I)/2020 dated 15th May, 2020.

question: Schedule-I to the Public Procurement Rules, 2004 was inserted vide which S.R.O., and when?
correctAnswer: S.R.O. No. 140(I)/2021 dated 2nd February, 2024
explanation: Schedule-I was inserted vide S.R.O. No. 140(I)/2021 dated 2nd February, 2024 (as noted in the document, despite the SRO number's year prefix).

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the minimum response time (from advertisement) for Agricultural Products (Fertilizer, Grains and Sugar)?
correctAnswer: Seven days
explanation: Schedule-I lists a minimum response time of seven days for agricultural products (Fertilizer, Grains, and Sugar).

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the minimum bid validity period (after issuance of evaluation report) for Agricultural Products?
correctAnswer: Three days
explanation: Schedule-I sets a minimum three-day bid validity period after the evaluation report for agricultural products.

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the minimum response time for Petroleum Products (e.g., MOGAS, HSD, Jet Fuel, Furnace Oil)?
correctAnswer: Three days
explanation: Schedule-I lists a minimum response time of three days for the listed petroleum products.

question: Under Schedule-I, the grievance period (after filing of grievance) is uniformly set at how many days for Agricultural Products, Petroleum Products, and Coal?
correctAnswer: One day
explanation: Schedule-I sets a uniform one-day grievance period for agricultural products, petroleum products, and coal (sub-bituminous).

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the minimum response time for Coal (Sub-bituminous)?
correctAnswer: Three days
explanation: Schedule-I lists a minimum response time of three days for sub-bituminous coal.

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the minimum response time (from advertisement) for LNG/LPG — notably shorter than other listed commodities?
correctAnswer: Twenty-four hours
explanation: Schedule-I sets a distinctly short minimum response time of twenty-four hours for LNG/LPG, reflecting the urgency of that market.

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the minimum bid validity period for LNG/LPG after issuance of the evaluation report?
correctAnswer: Eight hours
explanation: Schedule-I sets the LNG/LPG bid validity period at a minimum of eight hours, far shorter than other commodities given market volatility.

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the maximum period restraining signing of contract (after issuance of evaluation report) for LNG/LPG?
correctAnswer: Three hours
explanation: Schedule-I sets this restraining period at a minimum of three hours for LNG/LPG (column 7).

question: Under Schedule-I, what is the grievance redressal period (after filing of grievance) for LNG/LPG?
correctAnswer: Four hours
explanation: Schedule-I sets the grievance redressal period for LNG/LPG at four hours, reflecting the commodity's market volatility and urgency.

question: Schedule-I as reproduced in the Gazette of Pakistan was signed by which Section Officer?
correctAnswer: Maria Azhar
explanation: The Gazette notification for Schedule-I was signed by Maria Azhar, Section Officer (RA-III).

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: What is the short title of these regulations under Regulation 1?
options: Financial Management and Powers of Principal Accounting Officers Regulations, 2021
correctAnswer: Financial Management and Powers of Principal Accounting Officers Regulations, 2021
explanation: Regulation 1 gives the short title as the Financial Management and Powers of Principal Accounting Officers Regulations, 2021.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 1, to which entities do these regulations apply?
options: All Federal Government Ministries, Divisions, attached departments, subordinate offices, and entities functioning under existing rules, except Defence Services
correctAnswer: All Federal Government Ministries, Divisions, attached departments, subordinate offices, and entities functioning under existing rules, except Defence Services
explanation: Regulation 1 extends application to all Federal Government Ministries, Divisions, attached departments, subordinate offices, and entities under existing rules, with an express exception for Defence Services.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 2(2), how are terms not explicitly defined in these regulations to be interpreted?
options: Per Finance Division circulars issued after 2021
They shall have the same meaning as assigned in the Public Finance Management Act, 2019
correctAnswer: They shall have the same meaning as assigned in the Public Finance Management Act, 2019
explanation: Regulation 2(2) ties undefined terms to the meaning assigned in the Public Finance Management Act, 2019.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 3, what is the primary financial role of the Principal Accounting Officer (PAO)?
options: To approve only the annual budget
To represent Pakistan in international financial bodies
To be responsible for all financial matters relating to offices under their administrative control, acting as custodian and operator of financial resources
correctAnswer: To be responsible for all financial matters relating to offices under their administrative control, acting as custodian and operator of financial resources
explanation: Regulation 3 makes the PAO responsible for all financial matters of offices under their administrative control, acting as custodian and operator of financial resources.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 4, which of the following is a valid basis for designating an official as a PAO?
options: Being the head of a department/subordinate office, controlling a specific budgetary demand for grant, or controlling one or more cost centres involving strategic interest
Being nominated by the Cabinet Secretary alone
Being the most senior officer by age
correctAnswer: Being the head of a department/subordinate office, controlling a specific budgetary demand for grant, or controlling one or more cost centres involving strategic interest
explanation: Regulation 4 lists these criteria (head of department/office, controller of a budgetary demand for grant, or controller of strategic cost centres), with provisions for senior officers where the head holds a constitutional position.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 5, who designates a Principal Accounting Officer?
options: The Prime Minister, on the recommendation of the administrative Secretary of the concerned Division and the Finance Division
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister, on the recommendation of the administrative Secretary of the concerned Division and the Finance Division
explanation: Regulation 5 vests designation power in the Prime Minister, acting on the recommendation of the administrative Secretary and the Finance Division, which processes and notifies the case in the official Gazette.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 6, to whom is the Principal Accounting Officer accountable?
options: The Parliament of Pakistan, including all relevant Parliamentary Committees, for use of resources, regularity, and propriety of expenditure
The Chief Secretary of the Province
correctAnswer: The Parliament of Pakistan, including all relevant Parliamentary Committees, for use of resources, regularity, and propriety of expenditure
explanation: Regulation 6 makes the PAO accountable before Parliament (and its relevant Committees) for the use of resources and the regularity/propriety of expenditure from the budget, special fund, or public account.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(a) and (b), what core responsibilities regarding financial propriety and resource use are mandated for the PAO?
options: To enforce principles of financial propriety (compliance with laws, prudence, due diligence, value for money) and ensure effective, efficient, economical, and transparent use of funds, budget, assets, and human resources
correctAnswer: To enforce principles of financial propriety (compliance with laws, prudence, due diligence, value for money) and ensure effective, efficient, economical, and transparent use of funds, budget, assets, and human resources
explanation: Regulation 7(a) and (b) require enforcement of financial propriety principles and ensuring effective, efficient, economical, transparent use of resources.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(c) to (f), which of the following is an assigned duty of the PAO?
options: Assisting the chief finance and accounts officer, formulating plans for careful public service delivery, seeking prior Finance Division approval for non-delegated financial matters, and preparing budgetary proposals within agreed indicative budget ceilings
Chairing the Council of Common Interests
correctAnswer: Assisting the chief finance and accounts officer, formulating plans for careful public service delivery, seeking prior Finance Division approval for non-delegated financial matters, and preparing budgetary proposals within agreed indicative budget ceilings
explanation: Regulation 7(c)-(f) assigns these administrative and budgetary duties to the PAO.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(g) to (j), the PAO's responsibilities include firming up current/development budget proposals in executing agencies (keeping federal funds in relevant division demands if provincially executed), ensuring budgetary allocations for timely emoluments, properly accounting for foreign exchange transactions/ loans, and:
options: Realizing budgeted revenues (especially non-tax revenues) on time
correctAnswer: Realizing budgeted revenues (especially non-tax revenues) on time
explanation: Regulation 7(g)-(j) includes timely realization of budgeted revenues, especially non-tax revenues, among the PAO's core duties.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(k) to (p), the PAO's duties include executing budgets per government priorities, sanctioning expenditure within delegated powers, monitoring KPIs and internal controls with the chief internal auditor, ensuring safe custody and maximum returns on assets, and:
options: Conducting monthly reconciliations with accounting offices and submitting quarterly reconciled statements to the Finance Division
Approving the national budget in Parliament
correctAnswer: Conducting monthly reconciliations with accounting offices and submitting quarterly reconciled statements to the Finance Division
explanation: Regulation 7(k)-(p) requires monthly reconciliations with accounting offices and quarterly reconciled statements submitted to the Finance Division.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(q) to (u), the PAO's duties include ensuring grants-in-aid are non-recurring and approved after detailed review, controlling contingent liabilities and public entity salary/pension burdens, maintaining proper asset/liability and revenue/expenditure records, providing half-yearly statements for public entities, and:
options: Attending Public Accounts Committee (PAC) meetings and regularly holding Departmental Accounts Committee (DAC) meetings
correctAnswer: Attending Public Accounts Committee (PAC) meetings and regularly holding Departmental Accounts Committee (DAC) meetings
explanation: Regulation 7(q)-(u) includes attending PAC meetings and regularly holding DAC meetings among the PAO's governance responsibilities.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(2), what reporting obligation applies to designated principal accounting officers OTHER than a Division Secretary?
options: They report only at the end of their tenure
They report directly to the Auditor-General only

They must submit monthly, quarterly, and annual reports regarding the exercise of their financial powers to the Secretary of the administrative Division, through the chief finance and accounts officer
correctAnswer: They must submit monthly, quarterly, and annual reports regarding the exercise of their financial powers to the Secretary of the administrative Division, through the chief finance and accounts officer
explanation: Regulation 7(2) requires such PAOs to submit monthly/quarterly/annual reports on the exercise of financial powers to the administrative Division's Secretary, via the chief finance and accounts officer.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(3) to (5), what joint accountability applies to PAOs, heads of departments, and autonomous bodies?
options: PAOs, heads of departments, and autonomous bodies are jointly and severally responsible for financial propriety and expenditure control
No joint accountability exists; each is independently liable
Only the PAO is accountable, heads of departments are exempt
Only the Finance Division is accountable
correctAnswer: PAOs, heads of departments, and autonomous bodies are jointly and severally responsible for financial propriety and expenditure control
explanation: Regulation 7(3)-(5) establishes joint and several responsibility of PAOs, heads of departments, and autonomous bodies for financial propriety and expenditure control, alongside reporting requirements for subordinate officers exercising delegated powers.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 7(6) and (7), what institutional change was made regarding the Financial Advisor's organization, and what principle governs delegation of financial powers?
options: The Financial Advisor's organization of the Finance Division has been disbanded (with Joint/Deputy Secretaries Expenditures reassigned duties); the Finance Division retains overarching financial business, and expenditures sanctioned under delegated powers do not require endorsement from Finance or Establishment Divisions respectively
Financial Advisors were transferred to the Auditor-General's office
The Financial Advisor's powers were expanded to all Ministries
A new Financial Advisor's Wing was created
correctAnswer: The Financial Advisor's organization of the Finance Division has been disbanded (with Joint/Deputy Secretaries Expenditures reassigned duties); the Finance Division retains overarching financial business, and expenditures sanctioned under delegated powers do not require endorsement from Finance or Establishment Divisions respectively
explanation: Regulations 7(6)-(7) disband the Financial Advisor's organization, reassign duties to Joint/ Deputy Secretaries Expenditures, and establish that delegated-power expenditures don't require separate Finance/ Establishment Division endorsement, while heads remain accountable for delegated limits.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 9, what standard of financial prudence must a PAO exercise over public funds?
options: A standard set solely by the Auditor-General
The same vigilance as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise over their own money
Only compliance with the annual budget
correctAnswer: The same vigilance as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise over their own money
explanation: Regulation 9 requires PAOs to exercise the same vigilance over public funds as a person of ordinary prudence would over their own money.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 10, public funds must deliver services:
options: With maximum speed regardless of cost
correctAnswer: Efficiently, with reduced waste
explanation: Regulation 10 mandates that PAOs ensure public funds deliver services efficiently with reduced waste.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 11, funds must provide public advantage without conferring direct or indirect personal or selective benefits, EXCEPT when:
correctAnswer: Court-ordered or policy-backed
explanation: Regulation 11 permits personal/selective benefits only where court-ordered or policy-backed; otherwise funds must serve public advantage without such benefits.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 12, allowances (such as traveling allowances) must be regulated so that they:
options: Do not become a source of profit
Are paid only in foreign currency
correctAnswer: Do not become a source of profit
explanation: Regulation 12 requires allowances to be regulated so they do not become a source of profit for the recipient.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 13, PAOs and heads of departments must delegate appropriate financial powers to subordinate officers/officials, especially those providing public services or infrastructure investments, while:
options: Requiring Cabinet approval for every delegation
Eliminating the need for any further reporting
Adhering to financial propriety, without diminishing the PAO's overall oversight responsibility and accountability
Transferring all oversight responsibility to the subordinate
correctAnswer: Adhering to financial propriety, without diminishing the PAO's overall oversight responsibility and accountability
explanation: Regulation 13 requires such delegation to adhere to financial propriety, but the PAO's overall oversight responsibility and accountability is NOT diminished by delegating powers.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 14(a)-(c), no expenditure can be incurred or committed without sanction from a competent authority and provision in the schedule of authorized expenditure, supplementary grant, or re- appropriation under which section of the Act?
correctAnswer: Section 11
explanation: Regulation 14(a)-(c) ties expenditure sanction to provision under Section 11 of the (Public Finance Management) Act.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 14, by what date each year may PAOs approve re-appropriations within the same budget grant (extendable by the Finance Division in exigencies)?
correctAnswer: May 31st
explanation: Regulation 14 sets May 31st each year as the deadline for PAO-approved re-appropriations within the same budget grant.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 14, due diligence must be exercised to avoid creating future liabilities on heads like pay, pensions, utilities, or rents, and requests for supplementary budgets for re-appropriated heads:
options: Are approved only for defence-related heads
correctAnswer: Will not be entertained
explanation: Regulation 14 states that requests for supplementary budgets for re-appropriated heads will not be entertained.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 14(d)-(h), Ministries, Divisions, and subordinate bodies must surrender anticipated savings to the Finance Division by which date each year?
correctAnswer: May 31st
explanation: Regulation 14(d)-(h) requires surrender of anticipated savings to the Finance Division by May 31st each year.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 14(d)-(h), public procurements must be conducted under which law/rules?
correctAnswer: The PPRA Ordinance and rules
explanation: Regulation 14(d)-(h) requires procurement of goods and services under the PPRA (Public Procurement Regulatory Authority) Ordinance and rules.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 14(d)-(h), development schemes must be implemented in abidance with instructions issued by which body?
correctAnswer: The Planning Commission
explanation: Regulation 14(d)-(h) requires abidance with Planning Commission instructions for development schemes.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 15, the Finance Division's responsibilities regarding budget and expenditure are mandated by the Constitution of Pakistan, the Federal Responsibility and Debt Limitation Act, 2005, and which other Act?
correctAnswer: The Public Finance Management Act, 2019
explanation: Regulation 15 references the Public Finance Management Act, 2019, alongside the Constitution and the Federal Responsibility and Debt Limitation Act, 2005, as the mandate for Finance Division's budget/expenditure responsibilities.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 16, when must the Finance Division be consulted regarding financial matters of Ministries or Divisions?
options: In accordance with the Rules of Business, 1973, on matters including costing, contingent liabilities, future budget implications, cash forecasting, financing modalities, and financial authorities/powers
Only during the annual budget cycle
Only when expenditure exceeds Rs. 1 billion
correctAnswer: In accordance with the Rules of Business, 1973, on matters including costing, contingent liabilities, future budget implications, cash forecasting, financing modalities, and financial authorities/powers
explanation: Regulation 16 requires Finance Division consultation per the Rules of Business, 1973, on a broad range of financial matters as listed.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 17, the Finance Division is empowered to issue policy guidelines and instructions covering funds-release strategies, austerity measures, commitment control systems, internal controls, internal audit charters, delegation of powers, and:
options: Assignment or revolving fund account procedures
correctAnswer: Assignment or revolving fund account procedures
explanation: Regulation 17 includes assignment or revolving fund account procedures among the matters covered by Finance Division policy guidelines.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 22, when and why may the Finance Division extend the deadline for re-appropriation of funds?
options: Only in the last quarter of the fiscal year
Upon request, the Finance Division may extend the date for re-appropriation of funds after the date specified under the Act
correctAnswer: Upon request, the Finance Division may extend the date for re-appropriation of funds after the date specified under the Act
explanation: Regulation 22 allows the Finance Division to extend the re-appropriation deadline upon request.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 23, under what conditions may surrendered funds be included in the next year's budget?
options: Never, surrendered funds are permanently lost

Where appropriate, the Finance Division may approve inclusion of an equal amount of surrendered funds in the next year's budget, specifically for development projects and programs of foreign-funded projects
correctAnswer: Where appropriate, the Finance Division may approve inclusion of an equal amount of surrendered funds in the next year's budget, specifically for development projects and programs of foreign-funded projects
explanation: Regulation 23 allows Finance Division approval for re-inclusion of an equal amount of surrendered funds, specifically for development projects and foreign-funded project programs.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 24, the Finance Division operates a monitoring unit for state-owned enterprises that maintains an electronic database of financial/operational performance, tracks investments, loans, and government guarantees, and:
options: Assesses fiscal risks and submits recommendations on performance and governance of state-owned enterprises
Directly manages the enterprises' daily operations
correctAnswer: Assesses fiscal risks and submits recommendations on performance and governance of state-owned enterprises
explanation: Regulation 24 tasks this monitoring unit with fiscal risk assessment and recommendations on SOE performance and governance.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 25, any lump provision required in the budget must form part of:
options: The demand for grants under the control of the Finance Division
correctAnswer: The demand for grants under the control of the Finance Division
explanation: Regulation 25 requires lump provisions to form part of the demand for grants under Finance Division control, with further allocations made only after completing financial and codal formalities.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulations 26 and 27, who approves the creation of posts and the appointment of contingent paid staff?
options: The Finance Division, strictly within budgetary provisions and per instructions issued from time to time
The concerned Ministry alone, without Finance Division involvement
correctAnswer: The Finance Division, strictly within budgetary provisions and per instructions issued from time to time
explanation: Regulations 26 and 27 assign approval of post creation and contingent paid staff appointment to the Finance Division, within budgetary provisions.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 28, on which official committees does the Finance Division maintain representation?
options: The Public Accounts Committee, Departmental Audit Committee, DDWP, CDWP, and ECNEC
Only the Senate Standing Committee on Finance
correctAnswer: The Public Accounts Committee, Departmental Audit Committee, DDWP, CDWP, and ECNEC
explanation: Regulation 28 lists PAC, Departmental Audit Committee, DDWP, CDWP, and ECNEC as committees where the Finance Division maintains representation through authorized officials.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 29, what role does the Finance Division play regarding development projects and schemes?
options: It provides opinions on financial matters related to development projects and schemes, in light of medium- term macroeconomic and fiscal frameworks
It directly implements all development projects
It has no role, this is solely the Planning Commission's function
It only reviews projects after completion
correctAnswer: It provides opinions on financial matters related to development projects and schemes, in light of medium- term macroeconomic and fiscal frameworks
explanation: Regulation 29 tasks the Finance Division with providing financial opinions on development projects/schemes, informed by medium-term macroeconomic and fiscal frameworks.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 30, who heads the office of the Chief Finance and Accounts Officer (CFAO)?
options: A retired civil servant on contract
A senior-level officer responsible for assisting and supporting the principal accounting officer in managing financial affairs
A junior officer selected by rotation
correctAnswer: A senior-level officer responsible for assisting and supporting the principal accounting officer in managing financial affairs
explanation: Regulation 30 establishes the CFAO's office as headed by a senior-level officer who assists and supports the PAO in managing financial affairs.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(a), what governing rules and manuals must the CFAO's office follow?
options: The Public Finance Management Act, manuals, regulations, instructions, and guidelines issued by the Finance Division
correctAnswer: The Public Finance Management Act, manuals, regulations, instructions, and guidelines issued by the Finance Division
explanation: Regulation 31(a) requires the CFAO's office to follow the PFM Act and Finance Division manuals/regulations/instructions/guidelines.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(b), which grade of officers is generally eligible for posting as a CFAO?
options: BPS-20 officers, or senior BPS-19 officers of the Pakistan Audit and Accounts Service (PAAS) on their own pay scale if BPS-20 is unavailable
correctAnswer: BPS-20 officers, or senior BPS-19 officers of the Pakistan Audit and Accounts Service (PAAS) on their own pay scale if BPS-20 is unavailable
explanation: Regulation 31(b) sets BPS-20 as the general eligibility grade, with BPS-19 PAAS officers eligible on their own pay scale if BPS-20 is unavailable.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(c), which authority notifies the posting of a CFAO for a Ministry or Division?
options: The Establishment Division, in consultation with the Auditor General of Pakistan
correctAnswer: The Establishment Division, in consultation with the Auditor General of Pakistan
explanation: Regulation 31(c) assigns this notification role to the Establishment Division, acting in consultation with the Auditor General of Pakistan.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(c), what is the initial duration of a CFAO's posting, and can it be extended?
options: An initial period of not less than two years, extendable to another period of two years
correctAnswer: An initial period of not less than two years, extendable to another period of two years
explanation: Regulation 31(c) sets the initial CFAO posting period at not less than two years, extendable for another two years.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(d), which additional charges are prohibited for a CFAO, and what post-tenure restriction applies?
options: The CFAO must resign after one term
The CFAO cannot hold additional charges as Joint Secretary, Deputy Secretary, or chief internal auditor, and cannot serve as external auditor for that Ministry for three years
The CFAO cannot ever be promoted
correctAnswer: The CFAO cannot hold additional charges as Joint Secretary, Deputy Secretary, or chief internal auditor, and cannot serve as external auditor for that Ministry for three years
explanation: Regulation 31(d) bars these additional charges and imposes a three-year post-tenure restriction on serving as external auditor for that Ministry.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(e), to whom must a CFAO directly report and work under supervision?
options: Directly to and under the supervision of the Secretary of the Ministry or Division (the principal accounting officer)
correctAnswer: Directly to and under the supervision of the Secretary of the Ministry or Division (the principal accounting officer)
explanation: Regulation 31(e) requires the CFAO to report directly to, and work under the supervision of, the Ministry/Division Secretary (PAO).

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(f), under what condition may a CFAO be transferred before completing their prescribed tenure?
options: Upon the written advice of the PAO or Finance Division to the Auditor General of Pakistan, for failing to discharge functions satisfactorily
At the CFAO's own discretion at any time
correctAnswer: Upon the written advice of the PAO or Finance Division to the Auditor General of Pakistan, for failing to discharge functions satisfactorily
explanation: Regulation 31(f) permits early transfer only upon written advice from the PAO or Finance Division to the Auditor General, based on unsatisfactory performance.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(g), how are the pay and allowances of a CFAO funded?
options: From a separate central CFAO fund
Split equally between the Ministry and Finance Division
They are on the payroll of the Ministry or Division concerned, with all related expenditures charged to that Ministry/Division
correctAnswer: They are on the payroll of the Ministry or Division concerned, with all related expenditures charged to that Ministry/Division
explanation: Regulation 31(g) places CFAO pay/allowances on the payroll of, and charged to, the Ministry or Division concerned.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(h), which authority decides any addition or reduction in the existing sanctioned posts of CFAOs?
options: The Auditor General of Pakistan, in consultation with the Finance Division and Establishment Division
correctAnswer: The Auditor General of Pakistan, in consultation with the Finance Division and Establishment Division
explanation: Regulation 31(h) assigns this decision to the Auditor General of Pakistan, in consultation with the Finance and Establishment Divisions.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(i), who initiates or writes the performance evaluation report (PER) of a CFAO?
options: The Secretary of the Division concerned
correctAnswer: The Secretary of the Division concerned
explanation: Regulation 31(i) assigns initiation of the CFAO's PER to the Secretary of the Division concerned.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(j), which internal officers responsible for budget and accounts must work under and report to the CFAO?
options: The Deputy Secretary (or equivalent) and Section Officer (or equivalent) responsible for budget, finance, and accounts
correctAnswer: The Deputy Secretary (or equivalent) and Section Officer (or equivalent) responsible for budget, finance, and accounts
explanation: Regulation 31(j) places the Deputy Secretary/equivalent and Section Officer/equivalent (handling budget, finance, and accounts) under the CFAO's supervision.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 31(k), who decides matters relating to the posting of subordinate officers as deputy or assistant CFAOs?
options: The Secretary (principal accounting officer) of the Ministry or Division concerned
correctAnswer: The Secretary (principal accounting officer) of the Ministry or Division concerned
explanation: Regulation 31(k) vests this decision with the Secretary (PAO) of the Ministry or Division concerned.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(1)(a), what is the CFAO's role in budget planning and coordination?
options: To coordinate the entire budgeting activity in the Division, departments, subordinate offices, and organizations under the Division, undertaking budget planning and execution
To approve the budget without PAO involvement
To act only as a passive record-keeper
To independently set the national budget
correctAnswer: To coordinate the entire budgeting activity in the Division, departments, subordinate offices, and organizations under the Division, undertaking budget planning and execution
explanation: Regulation 32(1)(a) tasks the CFAO with coordinating the entire budgeting activity across the Division and its subordinate bodies.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(1)(b) and (c), what financial elements must the CFAO consider during budget preparation?
options: Revenues/receipts generated by various organizations, all accrued liabilities of previous years, estimation of resources, financial implications of operations/schemes, and budgets for asset repair and maintenance
correctAnswer: Revenues/receipts generated by various organizations, all accrued liabilities of previous years, estimation of resources, financial implications of operations/schemes, and budgets for asset repair and maintenance
explanation: Regulation 32(1)(b)-(c) requires consideration of revenues, accrued liabilities, resource estimation, financial implications of operations, and asset repair/maintenance budgets.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(1)(d), how must the CFAO ensure the quality and accuracy of budget estimates?
options: By ensuring estimates are realistic, finalized after proper deliberations, and prepared in accordance with canons of propriety, enactments, rules, and Finance Division instructions
By outsourcing estimation to private consultants
By copying the previous year's figures
By relying solely on verbal instructions from the Minister
correctAnswer: By ensuring estimates are realistic, finalized after proper deliberations, and prepared in accordance with canons of propriety, enactments, rules, and Finance Division instructions
explanation: Regulation 32(1)(d) requires realistic estimates, proper deliberation, and compliance with canons of propriety, enactments, rules, and Finance Division instructions.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(1)(e), what duties does the CFAO perform regarding mid-year reports, Indicative Budget Ceilings (IBC), and Budget Call Circulars?
options: No duties, this is solely the PAO's function
Only archiving old Budget Call Circulars

Assisting the PAO in submitting mid-year reports, distributing/allocating funds under various heads upon receiving IBCs per Budget Call Circular guidelines, and reporting to the Finance Division within timelines
correctAnswer: Assisting the PAO in submitting mid-year reports, distributing/allocating funds under various heads upon receiving IBCs per Budget Call Circular guidelines, and reporting to the Finance Division within timelines
explanation: Regulation 32(1)(e) assigns these mid-year reporting and fund allocation duties to the CFAO.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(1)(f), what responsibilities does the CFAO have concerning Budget Orders and New Item Statements (BOs/NIS)?
options: No responsibility, these are handled by Finance Division staff directly
Overseeing and authenticating preparation of BOs and NIS pertaining to the Division and its offices, ensuring timely submission to the Finance Division
Only reviewing BOs after they are finalized
correctAnswer: Overseeing and authenticating preparation of BOs and NIS pertaining to the Division and its offices, ensuring timely submission to the Finance Division
explanation: Regulation 32(1)(f) tasks the CFAO with overseeing/authenticating BO and NIS preparation and ensuring timely Finance Division submission.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(1)(g), how does the CFAO handle budgetary proposals received from subordinate departments or autonomous bodies?
options: By forwarding them unreviewed to the Finance Division
By rejecting proposals exceeding a fixed limit without review

By examining all development and non-development budgetary proposals/estimates received from heads of departments, subordinate offices, or autonomous bodies, and furnishing advice with the PAO's approval
correctAnswer: By examining all development and non-development budgetary proposals/estimates received from heads of departments, subordinate offices, or autonomous bodies, and furnishing advice with the PAO's approval
explanation: Regulation 32(1)(g) requires the CFAO to examine such proposals and furnish advice, with the PAO's approval.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(2)(a) and (b), what are the CFAO's responsibilities regarding non-tax revenue estimation and laws?
options: Assisting the PAO in the policy and administration of non-tax revenue laws, and examining revenue receipt estimates against previous collections, variance justifications, and rules
correctAnswer: Assisting the PAO in the policy and administration of non-tax revenue laws, and examining revenue receipt estimates against previous collections, variance justifications, and rules
explanation: Regulation 32(2)(a)-(b) assigns the CFAO a role in non-tax revenue law administration and examination of revenue estimates.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(2)(c), how must the CFAO manage revenue reconciliation, outstanding recoveries, and legal cases?
options: Ensuring revenues are budgeted/reported/reconciled under correct heads, initiating action and informing the Finance Division for outstanding dues recovery, and participating in litigation teams for court cases regarding revenues or dues
Delegating all revenue matters to the Attorney General
Ignoring outstanding dues below a certain threshold
correctAnswer: Ensuring revenues are budgeted/reported/reconciled under correct heads, initiating action and informing the Finance Division for outstanding dues recovery, and participating in litigation teams for court cases regarding revenues or dues
explanation: Regulation 32(2)(c) requires proper revenue reconciliation, recovery action/reporting, and litigation team participation for revenue-related court cases.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(2)(d) and (e), what duties apply to at-source adjustments and collection monitoring of non-tax revenues?
options: Delegating all monitoring to external auditors

Ensuring at-source adjustment of non-tax revenue receipts where applicable, and monitoring collection/ reconciliation of non-tax revenues across all departments/organizations under the PAO's jurisdiction (except the FBR)
correctAnswer: Ensuring at-source adjustment of non-tax revenue receipts where applicable, and monitoring collection/ reconciliation of non-tax revenues across all departments/organizations under the PAO's jurisdiction (except the FBR)
explanation: Regulation 32(2)(d)-(e) requires at-source adjustment where applicable and monitoring of non-tax revenue collection/reconciliation, explicitly excluding the FBR.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(3), what is the CFAO's function regarding economic forecasting?
options: Examining budget requirements and revenue estimations, analyzing financial strengths/weaknesses, and assisting the PAO in mapping the financial future and role in the overall economic picture
No forecasting function, this belongs to the Planning Commission alone
correctAnswer: Examining budget requirements and revenue estimations, analyzing financial strengths/weaknesses, and assisting the PAO in mapping the financial future and role in the overall economic picture
explanation: Regulation 32(3) tasks the CFAO with financial analysis and assisting the PAO in economic/ financial forecasting for the Division.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(4)(a) to (c), what duties does the CFAO carry out concerning domestic and foreign loans and grants?
options: Assessing financial needs for domestic/foreign loans and grants in coordination with concerned officers, maintaining records of receipt/payment schedules for periodic reporting, and preparing comprehensive financing proposals for the PAO's approval while following up with relevant agencies
Directly negotiating loan terms with foreign governments independently
correctAnswer: Assessing financial needs for domestic/foreign loans and grants in coordination with concerned officers, maintaining records of receipt/payment schedules for periodic reporting, and preparing comprehensive financing proposals for the PAO's approval while following up with relevant agencies
explanation: Regulation 32(4)(a)-(c) assigns these loan/grant assessment, record-keeping, and proposal preparation duties to the CFAO.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(5), what is the CFAO's role regarding investments?
options: Making investment decisions unilaterally without government rules
Proactively identifying investment opportunities, proposing investments per government rules after risk analysis, and providing guidance to entities
correctAnswer: Proactively identifying investment opportunities, proposing investments per government rules after risk analysis, and providing guidance to entities
explanation: Regulation 32(5) tasks the CFAO with proactive investment identification, risk-analyzed proposals per government rules, and guidance to entities.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(6)(a), how does the CFAO assist with development planning?
options: By working on development programs and engaging with the Planning Commission regarding the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP)
By only tracking PSDP expenditure after project completion
By independently approving all PSDP schemes
correctAnswer: By working on development programs and engaging with the Planning Commission regarding the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP)
explanation: Regulation 32(6)(a) requires the CFAO to work on development programs and engage with the Planning Commission on PSDP matters.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(6)(a) (continued), what support does the CFAO provide to planning teams?
options: Information on assets, resources, financing modes, cost estimates, and post-completion operational costs
No support, this is outside the CFAO's mandate
Only legal opinions on land acquisition
correctAnswer: Information on assets, resources, financing modes, cost estimates, and post-completion operational costs
explanation: Regulation 32(6)(a) requires the CFAO to provide planning teams with information on assets, resources, financing modes, cost estimates, and post-completion operational costs.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(6)(b), what analysis must the CFAO perform during project implementation?
options: Assessing cost and project impacts resulting from implementation variations or delays
correctAnswer: Assessing cost and project impacts resulting from implementation variations or delays
explanation: Regulation 32(6)(b) requires the CFAO to assess cost/project impacts arising from implementation variations or delays.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(6)(c), what guidelines must the CFAO follow for development projects?
options: Rules and instructions issued by the Planning and Development Division and Planning Commission
correctAnswer: Rules and instructions issued by the Planning and Development Division and Planning Commission
explanation: Regulation 32(6)(c) ties the CFAO's development-project conduct to Planning and Development Division/Planning Commission rules and instructions.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(7)(a), what role does the CFAO play in cash management, and what must be done with commercial bank accounts?
options: Delegating cash management entirely to commercial banks
Opening additional commercial bank accounts for flexibility
No cash management role; commercial accounts remain unaffected

Assisting the PAO in implementing the Cash Management and Treasury Single Account (TSA) Rules, 2020, including closing commercial bank accounts of the Ministry and transferring funds into the Federal Consolidated Fund
correctAnswer: Assisting the PAO in implementing the Cash Management and Treasury Single Account (TSA) Rules, 2020, including closing commercial bank accounts of the Ministry and transferring funds into the Federal Consolidated Fund
explanation: Regulation 32(7)(a) requires CFAO assistance in implementing the Cash Management and TSA Rules, 2020, including closure of commercial bank accounts and fund transfer into the Federal Consolidated Fund.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(8)(b), how does the CFAO monitor fund availability?
options: Monitoring accounts to ensure no shortfalls or excesses, especially under employee-related expenditure
Delegating all monitoring to the Auditor-General
correctAnswer: Monitoring accounts to ensure no shortfalls or excesses, especially under employee-related expenditure
explanation: Regulation 32(8)(b) requires ongoing monitoring of accounts for shortfalls/excesses, with particular attention to employee-related expenditure.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(8)(b), with which entities must accounts be reconciled on a monthly basis?
options: AGPR, banks, Finance Division, Economic Affairs Division, or development partners
correctAnswer: AGPR, banks, Finance Division, Economic Affairs Division, or development partners
explanation: Regulation 32(8)(b) requires monthly reconciliation with AGPR, banks, the Finance Division, Economic Affairs Division, or development partners, as applicable.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(8)(c), how often must expenditure and receipt statements be furnished to the PAO and Finance Division?
options: Monthly statements of expenditure and receipts, plus quarterly trend reports on excesses and savings
Only quarterly, with no monthly requirement
correctAnswer: Monthly statements of expenditure and receipts, plus quarterly trend reports on excesses and savings
explanation: Regulation 32(8)(c) requires monthly expenditure/receipt statements and quarterly trend reports on excesses and savings.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(9)(a), what is the CFAO's responsibility regarding asset protection?
options: Collaborating with officers to ensure financial and other assets are properly recorded, maintained, and guarded
Delegating asset protection entirely to security contractors
correctAnswer: Collaborating with officers to ensure financial and other assets are properly recorded, maintained, and guarded
explanation: Regulation 32(9)(a) requires CFAO collaboration to ensure assets are properly recorded, maintained, and guarded.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(9)(b), what is the CFAO's duty regarding annual asset stocktaking?
options: Being part of the team or supervising annual asset stocktaking and reporting annually to the PAO on asset status
Conducting stocktaking only once every five years
Delegating all stocktaking to external auditors
correctAnswer: Being part of the team or supervising annual asset stocktaking and reporting annually to the PAO on asset status
explanation: Regulation 32(9)(b) requires the CFAO's involvement in (or supervision of) annual asset stocktaking, with annual reporting to the PAO.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(10)(a), how does the CFAO assist with budget releases and re-appropriations?
options: By assisting the PAO and guiding officers in processing releases, re-appropriations, supplementary grants, surrenders, and post creation per budgetary policies
By only processing releases after year-end
By independently approving all releases without PAO involvement
correctAnswer: By assisting the PAO and guiding officers in processing releases, re-appropriations, supplementary grants, surrenders, and post creation per budgetary policies
explanation: Regulation 32(10)(a) tasks the CFAO with assisting and guiding officers on releases, re- appropriations, supplementary grants, surrenders, and post creation.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(10)(b), what role does the CFAO play in processing expenditure claims and bills?
options: Assisting concerned officers in processing claims and bills under the financial powers delegated to Ministries or Divisions
Approving all claims and bills personally without delegation
No processing role, this is solely for accounts staff
Rejecting all claims exceeding Rs. 1 million
correctAnswer: Assisting concerned officers in processing claims and bills under the financial powers delegated to Ministries or Divisions
explanation: Regulation 32(10)(b) assigns the CFAO an assisting role in processing claims/bills under delegated financial powers.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(10)(c), how does the CFAO monitor budget execution and liabilities?
options: By tracking expenditure only at fiscal year-end
No monitoring role for budget execution
By delegating this monitoring to the Auditor-General
By keeping quarterly expenditure within allocated budgets per Finance Division release strategies and monitoring the clearance of accrued liabilities and commitments
correctAnswer: By keeping quarterly expenditure within allocated budgets per Finance Division release strategies and monitoring the clearance of accrued liabilities and commitments
explanation: Regulation 32(10)(c) requires the CFAO to keep quarterly expenditure within allocated budgets and monitor clearance of accrued liabilities/commitments.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(10)(d), what action must the CFAO take regarding excess expenditures or missed payments?
options: Submitting timely cases to the PAO with remedial measures for excess expenditures, incorrect bookings, or resource shortages, while ensuring due payments are not missed
Delaying all payments until year-end reconciliation
correctAnswer: Submitting timely cases to the PAO with remedial measures for excess expenditures, incorrect bookings, or resource shortages, while ensuring due payments are not missed
explanation: Regulation 32(10)(d) requires timely case submission to the PAO with remedial measures, and ensuring due payments are not missed.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(11), what is the CFAO's responsibility regarding internal audit?
options: Cooperating with the Chief Internal Auditor (CIA) and audit committee to make annual audit plans, providing requisite records, submitting timely audit responses, and following up on audit recommendations
Only reviewing audit reports after they are finalized
Conducting internal audits personally, replacing the CIA
correctAnswer: Cooperating with the Chief Internal Auditor (CIA) and audit committee to make annual audit plans, providing requisite records, submitting timely audit responses, and following up on audit recommendations
explanation: Regulation 32(11) requires CFAO cooperation with the CIA and audit committee on planning, records, responses, and follow-up.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(12)(a), how does the CFAO assist with internal controls and checks?
options: Only reviewing controls once a year
Assisting the CIA in reviewing internal controls across budget, revenue, and expenditure areas, enforcing controls to prevent irregularities and fraud, and exercising internal checks
Delegating all internal control functions entirely to external auditors
correctAnswer: Assisting the CIA in reviewing internal controls across budget, revenue, and expenditure areas, enforcing controls to prevent irregularities and fraud, and exercising internal checks
explanation: Regulation 32(12)(a) requires CFAO assistance to the CIA in reviewing and enforcing internal controls to prevent irregularities and fraud.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(12)(b), what must the CFAO do upon noticing deviations from laws or rules?
options: Informing the PAO about deviations, following up on the PAO's orders, and working with the CIA to improve internal control suggestions
Take unilateral corrective action without informing anyone
Report directly to the Auditor-General without informing the PAO
correctAnswer: Informing the PAO about deviations, following up on the PAO's orders, and working with the CIA to improve internal control suggestions
explanation: Regulation 32(12)(b) requires informing the PAO, following up on orders, and collaborating with the CIA on internal control improvements.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(13), what are the CFAO's duties regarding risk management?
options: Assisting the PAO and CIA in annual risk assessments, maintaining a risk register, initiating risk response measures with PAO approval, and reviewing business processes to remove obstacles
Outsourcing all risk management to private consultants
correctAnswer: Assisting the PAO and CIA in annual risk assessments, maintaining a risk register, initiating risk response measures with PAO approval, and reviewing business processes to remove obstacles
explanation: Regulation 32(13) tasks the CFAO with risk assessment assistance, risk register maintenance, risk response initiation (with PAO approval), and business process review.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 32(14)(a), what is the CFAO's role in coordinating with the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and Departmental Accounts Committee (DAC)?
options: Coordinating all matters relating to the PAC, DAC, and audit observations on appropriation accounts, and ensuring compliance with PAC and DAC directives/recommendations
Attending PAC/DAC meetings only when personally summoned
Delegating all PAC/DAC coordination to the Auditor-General
correctAnswer: Coordinating all matters relating to the PAC, DAC, and audit observations on appropriation accounts, and ensuring compliance with PAC and DAC directives/recommendations
explanation: Regulation 32(14)(a) assigns the CFAO responsibility for coordinating PAC/DAC matters and ensuring compliance with their directives and recommendations.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3), who initiates the Performance Evaluation Report (PER) of the Chief Internal Auditor (CIA)?
options: The Secretary of the Division concerned (principal accounting officer), with countersigning decided in consultation with the Establishment Division
correctAnswer: The Secretary of the Division concerned (principal accounting officer), with countersigning decided in consultation with the Establishment Division
explanation: Regulation 33(3) assigns PER initiation for the CIA to the Division Secretary (PAO), with countersigning arrangements decided in consultation with the Establishment Division.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(2), who comprises the internal audit committee, and what is the CIA's role within it?
options: The PAO shall form an internal audit committee where the CIA serves as member/Secretary to consider, guide, and approve annual audit plans and review internal audit progress
The committee consists only of external consultants
The committee is external and the CIA has no role
The committee is chaired by the CIA, replacing the PAO's authority
correctAnswer: The PAO shall form an internal audit committee where the CIA serves as member/Secretary to consider, guide, and approve annual audit plans and review internal audit progress
explanation: Regulation 33(2) requires the PAO to form an internal audit committee, with the CIA serving as member/Secretary for audit planning, guidance, and progress review.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3)(a), what are the primary leadership and management duties of the Chief Internal Auditor?
options: Managing the Ministry's external public relations
Serving as head of internal audit staff, conducting audits directly, leading audit teams, and managing overall planning, execution, reporting, quality assurance, and follow-up
correctAnswer: Serving as head of internal audit staff, conducting audits directly, leading audit teams, and managing overall planning, execution, reporting, quality assurance, and follow-up
explanation: Regulation 33(3)(a) establishes these leadership/management duties for the CIA as head of internal audit.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3)(b) and (c), how must the CIA plan and execute internal audits?
options: By preparing annual risk-based internal audit plans for PAO approval, dividing them into executable segments, assigning tasks to team members, supervising audits, and ensuring professional ethics/codes of conduct are followed
By conducting audits only when specifically requested by the PAO
By outsourcing all audit planning to external firms
correctAnswer: By preparing annual risk-based internal audit plans for PAO approval, dividing them into executable segments, assigning tasks to team members, supervising audits, and ensuring professional ethics/codes of conduct are followed
explanation: Regulation 33(3)(b)-(c) requires risk-based annual audit plans (PAO-approved), task segmentation/assignment, supervision, and adherence to professional ethics.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3)(d) and (e), how are internal audit findings of a serious nature or confidential reports handled?
options: Findings are published publicly regardless of sensitivity
Findings are shared with all Ministry staff automatically
No confidentiality requirements apply to audit reports

Serious findings must be reported to the PAO as soon as possible for directions and compliance follow-up; reports must be kept strictly confidential, and sharing sensitive reports broadly requires prior PAO permission and possible redaction
correctAnswer: Serious findings must be reported to the PAO as soon as possible for directions and compliance follow-up; reports must be kept strictly confidential, and sharing sensitive reports broadly requires prior PAO permission and possible redaction
explanation: Regulation 33(3)(d)-(e) mandates prompt PAO reporting of serious findings and strict confidentiality, with PAO permission required for broader, possibly redacted, sharing.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3)(f), what responsibilities does the CIA have regarding staff development and co- opting members?
options: Delegating all staff development to the Establishment Division
Pointing out capacity-building opportunities for team members, striving for a balanced team, and co-opting Division officers as team members with prior PAO permission
Hiring and firing staff without any approval
correctAnswer: Pointing out capacity-building opportunities for team members, striving for a balanced team, and co-opting Division officers as team members with prior PAO permission
explanation: Regulation 33(3)(f) tasks the CIA with identifying capacity-building opportunities, maintaining team balance, and co-opting officers with PAO permission.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3)(g) to (i), what duties does the CIA perform concerning audit recommendations and internal controls?
options: Ensuring approved audit recommendations are carried out and monitored, reviewing internal controls in budget/revenue/expenditure/finance under the guidance of the CFAO and PAO, and assisting in enforcing controls to prevent fraud and waste
No follow-up duties after audit completion
Delegating all recommendation follow-up to external auditors
correctAnswer: Ensuring approved audit recommendations are carried out and monitored, reviewing internal controls in budget/revenue/expenditure/finance under the guidance of the CFAO and PAO, and assisting in enforcing controls to prevent fraud and waste
explanation: Regulation 33(3)(g)-(i) requires the CIA to ensure recommendations are implemented/ monitored and to review internal controls (under CFAO/PAO guidance) to prevent fraud/waste.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 33(3)(j) to (m), what actions must the CIA take regarding legal compliance, risk assessment, and control adjustments?
options: Ignoring risk assessment in favor of only financial reporting

Ensuring internal controls align with laws and ethics, informing the PAO of deviations, conducting annual risk assessments to maintain an internal audit risk register, initiating risk response measures with PAO approval, and assisting in adapting controls for specific situations
correctAnswer: Ensuring internal controls align with laws and ethics, informing the PAO of deviations, conducting annual risk assessments to maintain an internal audit risk register, initiating risk response measures with PAO approval, and assisting in adapting controls for specific situations
explanation: Regulation 33(3)(j)-(m) requires legal/ethical alignment of controls, PAO notification of deviations, annual risk assessments/register maintenance, and PAO-approved risk response measures.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Regulation 34, what previous rules, systems, and practices are repealed?
options: The revised System of Financial Control and Budgeting 2000, and any contrary regulations, instructions, or practices, except regarding Defence Services
Only the Public Finance Management Act, 2019
The Cash Management and TSA Rules, 2020
correctAnswer: The revised System of Financial Control and Budgeting 2000, and any contrary regulations, instructions, or practices, except regarding Defence Services
explanation: Regulation 34 repeals the revised System of Financial Control and Budgeting 2000 (and contrary regulations/instructions/practices), with an exception carved out for Defence Services, consistent with Regulation 1's scope.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under the FMP Regulations 2021, what powers are granted to Principal Accounting Officers regarding financial sanctions, as elaborated in the attached Schedules and Rules?
options: Unlimited sanctioning power with no budgetary constraint
Power to override the Finance Division's budget allocations at will
Power to reallocate funds between different Ministries without approval

To sanction expenditures within the allocated budget and delegated financial powers, ensuring that no expenditure is incurred without proper budgetary provision and prior sanction from a competent authority
correctAnswer: To sanction expenditures within the allocated budget and delegated financial powers, ensuring that no expenditure is incurred without proper budgetary provision and prior sanction from a competent authority
explanation: The Regulations (and their Schedule) confine PAO sanctioning power to the allocated budget and delegated financial powers, with mandatory prior sanction and budgetary provision for any expenditure.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under the FMP Regulations 2021, what general principle governs the financial powers of subordinate offices and attached departments?
options: They may exercise any financial power they consider appropriate
They have no financial powers under any circumstances
They must exercise only those financial powers expressly delegated to them by the PAO or through the schedules, while remaining fully accountable for financial propriety
Their financial powers are set solely by the Auditor-General, independent of the PAO
correctAnswer: They must exercise only those financial powers expressly delegated to them by the PAO or through the schedules, while remaining fully accountable for financial propriety
explanation: The Regulations restrict subordinate offices/attached departments to expressly delegated financial powers (via the PAO or schedules), while holding them fully accountable for financial propriety.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 1, what powers do Secretaries of Ministries/Divisions have regarding creation of temporary posts in Development Expenditure?
options: Powers limited to five posts per project
Powers only for posts below BPS-10

Full powers to create new posts in Development Expenditure/PSDP included in PC-I or PC-II after project approval by the relevant forum, subject to development budget availability against Employee Related Expenses (ERE) on a year-to-year basis until project completion
No powers, this requires Cabinet approval

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 1, when do posts created in development expenditure cease to exist?

Automatically upon the closure or completion of the project
Only when the Secretary issues a specific abolition order

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 1, what procedure applies to convert essential posts from development expenditure to current expenditure upon project completion?

Conversion requires a fresh Cabinet decision

Automatic conversion with no approval needed

explanation: Schedule Item 1 requires PC-IV submission, followed by MS Wing (Establishment Division) recommendation and Finance Division approval, for such conversion.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 1, what special requirement applies to proposals for creating posts belonging to occupational groups or services?
options: Proposals must first be referred to the concerned Division or Office for clearance before submitting them to the Finance Division
They require Prime Minister approval directly
correctAnswer: Proposals must first be referred to the concerned Division or Office for clearance before submitting them to the Finance Division
explanation: Schedule Item 1 requires prior clearance from the concerned Division/Office before such proposals reach the Finance Division.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 1, what power does the Head of Foreign Missions have regarding temporary post creation, and for what maximum duration?
options: No power to create temporary posts
Power limited to 30 days for any administrative purpose
Full power to create permanent posts abroad

correctAnswer: The Head of Foreign Missions may create a temporary post for a maximum period of 5 days, to enable a transferred official to brief and hand over accountable documents to an incoming official
explanation: Schedule Item 1 permits Heads of Foreign Missions to create a temporary post for up to 5 days specifically for handover/briefing purposes during official transfers.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 2, what are the conditions for converting a temporary post into a permanent post?
options: Any temporary post may be converted after six months

Secretaries of Ministries/Divisions have full powers if the posts have been in continuous existence for 5 years or more, were created for work of a permanent nature, and are likely to continue for an indefinite period
Conversion requires a fresh recruitment process
correctAnswer: Secretaries of Ministries/Divisions have full powers if the posts have been in continuous existence for 5 years or more, were created for work of a permanent nature, and are likely to continue for an indefinite period
explanation: Schedule Item 2 sets three cumulative conditions: 5+ years of continuous existence, permanent-nature work, and indefinite continuation likelihood.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 2, by what date must details of temporary posts converted into permanent posts during a financial year be reported to the Finance Division?
options: At the end of the financial year only
correctAnswer: Before October 1st every year

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 3, what powers do Secretaries have regarding the abolition of posts?
options: No powers; abolition requires Finance Division approval
Powers limited to development-budget posts only
Powers limited to posts vacant for less than one year
Full powers in both development and current budgets to abolish posts

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 3, what is the rule for posts that remain vacant for three years or more?

They remain active indefinitely with no consequence
They automatically convert to contract positions
They are automatically upgraded to a higher pay scale
correctAnswer: Any post that remains vacant for a period of 3 years or more is deemed to have been abolished and must be notified by the Division
explanation: Schedule Item 3 deems such long-vacant posts abolished, with mandatory notification by the Division.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 3, can a Secretary revive a post that has been deemed abolished due to a three- year vacancy?

Yes, but only with Cabinet ratification

correctAnswer: No, the powers for revival cannot be exercised by the Secretary of a Division without obtaining the prior approval of the Finance Division
explanation: Schedule Item 3 requires prior Finance Division approval before a Secretary may revive such a deemed-abolished post.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 4, what authority is granted for the reimbursement of medical charges?
options: Principal Accounting Officers, Heads of Departments, and Heads of Sub-ordinate offices all hold full powers, subject to the availability of the budget
No delegated authority; all cases go to the Finance Division
Only the Ministry of Health can sanction medical reimbursement
Only the PAO has this power
correctAnswer: Principal Accounting Officers, Heads of Departments, and Heads of Sub-ordinate offices all hold full powers, subject to the availability of the budget
explanation: Schedule Item 4 grants full powers to all three tiers (PAO, Heads of Departments, Heads of Sub-ordinate offices) for medical charge reimbursement, subject to budget availability.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 5, what general condition governs the re-appropriation of funds by PAOs, Heads of Departments, and Sub-ordinate offices?
options: They have full re-appropriation powers on the condition that funds remain available in all heads of accounts, especially in ERE (Employee Related Expenses), to ensure timely salary payments without creating liabilities or excess spending
Re-appropriation requires Cabinet approval in every instance
Only the PAO may re-appropriate; other tiers have no such power
correctAnswer: They have full re-appropriation powers on the condition that funds remain available in all heads of accounts, especially in ERE (Employee Related Expenses), to ensure timely salary payments without creating liabilities or excess spending
explanation: Schedule Item 5 grants full re-appropriation powers, conditioned on maintaining fund availability (especially in ERE) to ensure timely salaries without creating liabilities or overspending.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 5, General Instruction 5(A), what restrictions apply to re-appropriation from one demand to another or after the financial year?

Restrictions apply only to development expenditure, not current expenditure

correctAnswer: No re-appropriation may be made from one demand for grant to another, after the expiry of the financial year, or between funds authorized for expenditure charged on the Federal Consolidated Fund and other expenditures
explanation: General Instruction 5(A) bars these three types of re-appropriation: inter-demand, post- financial-year, and between Federal Consolidated Fund-charged expenditure and other expenditure.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 5, General Instruction 5(B), what items of expenditure cannot be met through re- appropriation?
options: There are no restrictions on the type of expenditure
Any item of expenditure un-sanctioned by a competent authority, or for a purpose whose allotment was specifically reduced or refused by the National Assembly
correctAnswer: Any item of expenditure un-sanctioned by a competent authority, or for a purpose whose allotment was specifically reduced or refused by the National Assembly
explanation: General Instruction 5(B) bars re-appropriation to fund unsanctioned expenditure items or items whose allotment was specifically reduced/refused by the National Assembly.

topic: Financial Management and Powers of PAOs Regulations 2021
question: Under Schedule Item 5, General Instruction 5(C), what prohibitions apply to re-appropriations between development and current expenditures or foreign exchange?
