question: Under the proviso inserted vide SRO 208(I)/2017, where the post of Head of an Organization is reserved for promotion and no suitable person is available, the appointing authority may fill the vacancy by initial appointment on:
options: Ad hoc basis for six months
correctAnswer: Open merit on contract basis
explanation: This proviso allows filling such a Head of Organization vacancy on open merit on contract basis where it is reserved for promotion but no suitable person is available.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 15, vacancies in posts in BPS 6 to 15 (and equivalent) in offices serving only a particular province or region shall be filled by appointment of persons:
options: Domiciled in the province or region concerned, strictly per the recruitment rules of the post
Selected purely on merit with no domicile requirement
correctAnswer: Domiciled in the province or region concerned, strictly per the recruitment rules of the post
explanation: APT Rule 15 restricts such appointments to persons domiciled in the concerned province/ region, per the applicable recruitment rules.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to APT Rule 15 (inserted vide SRO 791(I)/2020), vacancies in BPS 6-15 posts serving only the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) shall not, at any time by initial appointment, be filled less than what percentage from ICT-domiciled persons?
correctAnswer: Fifty percent
explanation: This proviso guarantees a minimum fifty percent share for ICT-domiciled persons in such ICT- serving posts.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 16, vacancies in posts in BPS 1 to 5 (and equivalent) shall ordinarily be filled on:
correctAnswer: Local basis
explanation: APT Rule 16 provides for such posts to ordinarily be filled on local basis.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to APT Rule 16 (inserted vide SRO 791(I)/2020), vacancies in BPS 1-5 posts in all offices situated within ICT shall not, at any time by initial appointment, be filled less than what percentage from ICT-domiciled persons?
correctAnswer: Fifty percent
explanation: This proviso guarantees at least fifty percent from ICT-domiciled persons for BPS 1-5 posts in ICT offices.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 17, a candidate for appointment must be in good mental and bodily health and free from any physical defect likely to interfere with:
correctAnswer: The discharge of his duties
explanation: APT Rule 17 requires good mental/bodily health and freedom from physical defects likely to interfere with duty discharge, subject to medical examination.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 18, when a post is required to be filled through the FPSC under the Federal Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 1978, the appointing authority shall forward a requisition to the Commission:
correctAnswer: Immediately, on the prescribed form
explanation: APT Rule 18 requires the appointing authority to forward a requisition to the Commission on a prescribed form immediately.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 18, in exceptional cases, an ad hoc appointment may be made for a period of:
options: One year or less, without any clearance
Six months or less, with prior clearance of the Commission
correctAnswer: Six months or less, with prior clearance of the Commission
explanation: APT Rule 18 allows ad hoc appointment for six months or less, with prior FPSC clearance as provided in Rule 19.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 19, when the appointing authority considers it in the public interest to urgently fill a post within Commission purview pending nomination, it may fill it on ad hoc basis for a period of six months or less after:
options: Simply notifying the Commission after the fact
Obtaining prior clearance of the Commission
correctAnswer: Obtaining prior clearance of the Commission
explanation: APT Rule 19 requires prior clearance of the Commission before making such an urgent ad hoc appointment.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 19, the post shall be advertised and the same procedures as laid down for initial appointment in which Part of the rules shall be followed for ad hoc appointments?
correctAnswer: Part III
explanation: APT Rule 19 requires following the Part III (Initial Appointment) procedures, including advertisement, for ad hoc appointments.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 20, short-term vacancies within Commission purview and vacancies from temporary posts (not exceeding six months) may be filled by the appointing authority otherwise than through the Commission, on:
options: A basis exempt from advertisement requirements
A purely temporary basis after advertising the vacancy
correctAnswer: A purely temporary basis after advertising the vacancy
explanation: APT Rule 20 permits filling such short-term/temporary vacancies on a purely temporary basis after advertisement, bypassing the Commission.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 20A(1) (inserted vide SRO 365(I)/2007), a person in the service of a Provincial Government (or an autonomous/semi-autonomous body etc.) possessing the prescribed minimum qualifications shall be eligible for appointment on deputation for a period not exceeding:
options: Three years, extendable for another period of two years
Indefinitely, at the lending organization's discretion
One year, extendable to two years
correctAnswer: Three years, extendable for another period of two years
explanation: APT Rule 20A(1) sets the initial deputation period at three years, extendable for another two years, on terms sanctioned by the appointing authority in consultation with the lending organization.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 20A(3), in case of appointment on deputation under sub-rule (1) or (2), pension contribution shall invariably be made by:
options: The Federal Government centrally, regardless of lending/borrowing status
correctAnswer: The borrowing organization
explanation: APT Rule 20A(3) requires the borrowing organization to invariably make the pension contribution.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to APT Rule 20A (inserted vide SRO 375(I)/2012), which categories are exempted from certain posting/deputation restrictions regarding co-location of spouses or residence near family?
options: Posting of serving husband and wife at the same station; unmarried female govt servants at parents'/family residence; married female govt servants at their husband's residence/posting (if husband not in govt employment)
correctAnswer: Posting of serving husband and wife at the same station; unmarried female govt servants at parents'/family residence; married female govt servants at their husband's residence/posting (if husband not in govt employment)
explanation: This proviso to APT Rule 20A provides these specific exemptions relating to spousal co- location and residence near family for female government servants.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 21(1) (Part V — Probation), persons appointed by initial appointment, promotion or transfer shall be on probation for a period of:
correctAnswer: One year
explanation: APT Rule 21(1) sets the standard probation period at one year for initial appointment, promotion, or transfer.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 21(2), the probation period may be curtailed for good and sufficient reasons, or extended for a period not exceeding:
correctAnswer: One year
explanation: APT Rule 21(2) allows extension of probation for a period not exceeding one year, as specified at the time of appointment.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 21(3), on successful completion of probation, the appointing authority shall:
options: By specific order, terminate the probation
Refer the matter to the FPSC for ratification
Take no action, as confirmation is automatic
correctAnswer: By specific order, terminate the probation
explanation: APT Rule 21(3) requires the appointing authority to terminate the probation by a specific order upon successful completion.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under APT Rule 21(4), if no order is issued under sub-rule (3) on the expiry of the first year of probation, the probation period shall be deemed to have been:
correctAnswer: Extended under sub-rule (2)
explanation: APT Rule 21(4) deems the probation period extended under sub-rule (2) if no order is issued by the end of the first year.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to APT Rule 21(4), read with Section 6(2) of the Civil Servants Act, 1973, in the absence of an order under sub-rule (3), the probation shall be deemed to have successfully been completed:
options: Never — an explicit order is always required
Only after a formal Cabinet review
On expiry of the extended period under sub-rule (2)
correctAnswer: On expiry of the extended period under sub-rule (2)
explanation: The proviso deems successful completion of probation upon expiry of the extended period under sub-rule (2), absent an explicit order.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: The Civil Servants (Service in International Organizations) Rules, 2016 were notified vide which SRO, and on what date?
correctAnswer: SRO 954(I)/2016, dated 7th October 2016
explanation: These rules were notified via SRO No. 954(I)/2016, dated the 7th October, 2016, by the Establishment Division.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 1(2) of the 2016 Rules, they apply to civil servants seeking employment on:
options: Reserved and specific posts, open posts, and deputation in any international organization
correctAnswer: Reserved and specific posts, open posts, and deputation in any international organization
explanation: Rule 1(2) applies these rules to reserved/specific posts, open posts, and deputation in international organizations, whether or not on behalf of Pakistan or with prior Federal Government permission.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(g), 'deputation' under these rules means:
options: A posting abroad for training only
Assignment of a civil servant to a post with prior approval of the competent authority, in an international organization
A leave of absence exceeding one year
correctAnswer: Assignment of a civil servant to a post with prior approval of the competent authority, in an international organization
explanation: Rule 2(1)(g) defines 'deputation' as assignment to a post in an international organization with prior approval of the competent authority.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(k), an 'open post' means a post open to all eligible competing candidates, including civil servants, that is:
options: Only available to BPS-20 and above officers
Restricted to a single occupational group
Not reserved for nomination by the Federal Government
Reserved for nomination by the Federal Government
correctAnswer: Not reserved for nomination by the Federal Government
explanation: Rule 2(1)(k) defines 'open post' as one open to all eligible candidates and NOT reserved for Federal Government nomination.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(l), a 'reserved and specific post' is one where occupancy is:
options: Limited to Pakistan's officials or alternates between Pakistan and other countries on their turn
correctAnswer: Limited to Pakistan's officials or alternates between Pakistan and other countries on their turn
explanation: Rule 2(1)(l) defines this as a post where occupancy is limited to Pakistan's officials or alternates on a turn basis with other countries.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(p), a 'static list' refers to a list of officers on deputation beyond how many years, approved under these rules?
correctAnswer: Five years
explanation: Rule 2(1)(p) defines 'static list' as a list of officers on deputation beyond five years, approved under these rules.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 3 (Bar to seek employment), a civil servant shall not approach an international organization for seeking employment without:
options: Approval of the Federal Government or, as the case may be, the competent authority
A No Objection Certificate from the Foreign Ministry only
Any prior clearance whatsoever, as this is unrestricted
correctAnswer: Approval of the Federal Government or, as the case may be, the competent authority
explanation: Rule 3 bars a civil servant from approaching an international organization without approval of the Federal Government or competent authority.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(a), for taking up an assignment in an international organization, a civil servant should have completed how many years of service in his cadre?
correctAnswer: Five years
explanation: Rule 4(1)(a) requires completion of five years of service in the civil servant's cadre for such an assignment.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(c) and (d), for reserved and specific posts, there shall be a written qualifying test organized by the concerned Ministry, with a minimum qualifying score set at:
correctAnswer: Sixty percent
explanation: Rule 4(1)(d) sets the minimum qualifying score in the written test at sixty percent.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(e), what weightage is given to the written test scores versus the interview scores?
correctAnswer: 80% written, 20% interview
explanation: Rule 4(1)(e) assigns eighty percent weightage to written test scores and twenty percent to interview scores.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(f), no minimum passing marks shall be fixed for the interview, and no candidate shall be deemed to have failed the selection process merely on the basis of:
correctAnswer: His performance in the interview
explanation: Rule 4(1)(f) prevents disqualification based solely on interview performance, since no minimum passing marks are fixed for it.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 4(1)(f), an officer nominated against a post of sensitive or strategic importance (as set out in the Schedule) shall be selected:
options: In a transparent manner to be determined by the competent authority
By the Prime Minister personally in every case
correctAnswer: In a transparent manner to be determined by the competent authority
explanation: This proviso requires transparent selection (as determined by the competent authority) for posts of sensitive/strategic importance.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 5(2), the case of a civil servant selected by an international organization for an open post shall be placed before which body for recommendation before sending to the competent authority?
correctAnswer: The Board (Special Selection Board)
explanation: Rule 5(2) requires such cases to be placed before the Board (Special Selection Board constituted under Rule 6) for recommendation.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(1), who is the Chairman of the Special Selection Board?
correctAnswer: Secretary, Cabinet Division
explanation: Rule 6(1)(a) designates the Secretary, Cabinet Division, as Chairman of the Special Selection Board.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(1), who serves as Member-cum-Secretary of the Special Selection Board?
correctAnswer: Joint Secretary (Training), Establishment Division
explanation: Rule 6(1)(e) designates the Joint Secretary (Training), Establishment Division, as Member- cum-Secretary.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(1), which Secretaries (besides the Chairman) are named as Members of the Special Selection Board?
options: Secretary, Commerce Division; Secretary, Planning Division
Secretary, Finance Division; Secretary, Law and Justice Division
Secretary, Interior Division; Secretary, Defence Division
Secretary, Establishment Division; Secretary, Economic Affairs Division; Secretary, Foreign Affairs Division
correctAnswer: Secretary, Establishment Division; Secretary, Economic Affairs Division; Secretary, Foreign Affairs Division
explanation: Rule 6(1)(b)-(d) name the Secretaries of Establishment Division, Economic Affairs Division, and Foreign Affairs Division as Members.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(2), a Secretary or representative not below which grade may be invited as a co-opted member of the Board?
correctAnswer: BS-21
explanation: Rule 6(2) allows co-option of a representative not below BS-21 as a co-opted member.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 7(1), who is the competent authority to approve deputation to international organizations for civil servants in BS-20 and above?
options: Secretary of the Ministry or Division concerned
correctAnswer: Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 7(1) Table Sl. No. 1 designates the Prime Minister as competent authority for BS-20 and above civil servants.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 7(1), who is the competent authority for civil servants in BS-17 to 19?
options: Secretary of the Ministry or Division concerned
correctAnswer: Secretary Establishment Division
explanation: Rule 7(1) Table Sl. No. 2 designates Secretary Establishment Division as competent authority for BS-17 to 19.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 7(1), who is the competent authority for civil servants in BS-1 to 16?
options: Secretary of the Ministry or Division concerned
correctAnswer: Secretary of the Ministry or Division concerned
explanation: Rule 7(1) Table Sl. No. 3 designates the Secretary of the Ministry or Division concerned as competent authority for BS-1 to 16.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 7(4), where a post for which recommendations have been formulated is abolished or withdrawn from circulation, the recommendations of the Board shall be deemed to have:
options: Been automatically transferred to another post
correctAnswer: Lapsed
explanation: Rule 7(4) deems the Board's recommendations to have lapsed if the post is abolished or withdrawn from circulation.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 8, a civil servant is ineligible to apply for permission under these rules if he is held guilty of misconduct/inefficiency under the Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973, or convicted of an offence of:
correctAnswer: Moral turpitude
explanation: Rule 8(a) bars eligibility for those held guilty of misconduct/inefficiency or convicted of an offence of moral turpitude.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 8(b), a civil servant is also ineligible if he has not completed how many years of service in his cadre after returning from an immediately preceding deputation to an international organization?
correctAnswer: Three years
explanation: Rule 8(b) requires completion of three years of service in cadre after returning from a preceding international deputation.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(1), the deputation shall be made initially for a period equal to:
options: A fixed three-year term regardless of the offer
The approved tenure of appointment offered by the borrowing international organization
correctAnswer: The approved tenure of appointment offered by the borrowing international organization
explanation: Rule 9(1) ties the initial deputation period to the tenure offered by the borrowing international organization.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(2), where the period of deputation is not specified, the default period shall be three years, extendable to a maximum additional period of:
correctAnswer: Two years
explanation: Rule 9(2) sets a default three-year period, extendable by a maximum of two more years with competent authority approval.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(3), in case of retention of a civil servant after expiry of the maximum period of five years, he shall be placed on:
correctAnswer: The static list
explanation: Rule 9(3) requires placement on the static list if retained beyond the maximum five-year period.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(4), the civil servant must execute a surety bond ensuring he will revert to the parent department on completion of tenure; in case of default, he becomes liable to be proceeded against for misconduct under which rules?
options: The Federal Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 1978
The Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973
correctAnswer: The Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973
explanation: Rule 9(4) ties default on the surety bond to misconduct proceedings under the Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: The Surety Bond form under these rules (see Rules 2 and 9) must be executed on a stamp paper of what value?
explanation: The Surety Bond form specifies execution on Stamp Paper of Rs. 100/-.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the Schedule to the 2016 Rules (see Rules 2 and 4), which of the following is listed as an International Organization of sensitive and strategic importance?
options: World Bank, IMF, ADB, IDB, and similar institutions
correctAnswer: World Bank, IMF, ADB, IDB, and similar institutions
explanation: The Schedule lists organizations such as World Bank, IMF, ADB, IDB, DFID, US-AID, OIC, ECO, IAEA, WTO, ICJ, SAARC Secretariat, Commonwealth Secretariat, WHO, ILO, OPEC, and IHRC as sensitive/ strategic.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under item 2 of the Schedule (amended vide SRO 1198(I)/2020), any post (other than an open post) offered to Pakistan under a bilateral or multilateral arrangement must be notified by the Establishment Division with the approval of:
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: Schedule item 2 requires such notification by the Establishment Division with the Prime Minister's approval.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: The Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020 were notified vide which SRO?
explanation: These rules were notified vide SRO No. 1331(I)/2020, dated 11th December 2020.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 1(2) of the Efficiency and Discipline Rules, 2020, these rules apply to:
options: Only officers in BS-20 and above
Only officers of the All-Pakistan Services
Only civil servants under disciplinary proceedings before 2020
correctAnswer: Every Civil Servant
explanation: Rule 1(2) states these rules come into force at once and apply to every Civil Servant.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(c) of the 2020 Rules, 'authority' means the appointing authority as prescribed in which rule?
options: Rule 9 of the Civil Servants Act, 1973
Rule 2 of the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1964
Rule 6 of the Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1973
correctAnswer: Rule 6 of the Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1973
explanation: Rule 2(1)(c) of the 2020 Rules defines 'authority' as the appointing authority per Rule 6 of the APT Rules, 1973.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the first proviso to Rule 2(1)(c), where proceedings are initiated against two or more civil servants jointly, the authority shall be determined in relation to:
options: The senior-most civil servant in rank, for all the accused
correctAnswer: The senior-most civil servant in rank, for all the accused
explanation: This proviso designates the authority in relation to the senior-most civil servant in rank as the authority for all the accused in joint proceedings.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the second proviso to Rule 2(1)(c), where the President or Prime Minister is the authority, all functions except which three specific functions shall be performed by the respective cadre administrator?
options: Approval of initiating disciplinary proceedings, appointment of a hearing officer, and final decision on the inquiry report
None — all functions are delegated to the cadre administrator
Recording evidence, cross-examination, and issuing show-cause notices
Framing of charges, suspension, and appeal disposal
correctAnswer: Approval of initiating disciplinary proceedings, appointment of a hearing officer, and final decision on the inquiry report
explanation: This proviso reserves approval of initiating proceedings, appointment of a hearing officer, and final decision on the inquiry report to the President/PM personally; other functions go to the cadre administrator.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(h), 'inefficiency' in relation to discharge of duties means:
options: Any single mistake made by a civil servant
The failure to efficiently perform functions assigned to him
correctAnswer: The failure to efficiently perform functions assigned to him
explanation: Rule 2(1)(h) defines 'inefficiency' as the failure to efficiently perform assigned functions.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(1)(k), 'misconduct' includes conduct prejudicial to good order or service discipline, or contrary to which Rules, and also includes acts to assert political/other exterior influence, or:
options: Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1964; also includes having entered a plea bargain and voluntarily returned assets/gains from corruption
Only acts committed while on foreign deputation
correctAnswer: Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1964; also includes having entered a plea bargain and voluntarily returned assets/gains from corruption
explanation: Rule 2(1)(k) defines misconduct broadly, referencing the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1964, improper influence-peddling, and voluntary return of corruptly acquired assets after a plea bargain.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 3(a) of the 2020 Rules, a civil servant is liable to be proceeded against if he is considered or reported to be:
options: On leave for an extended period
Inefficient or has ceased to be efficient
correctAnswer: Inefficient or has ceased to be efficient
explanation: Rule 3(a) makes inefficiency (or ceasing to be efficient) a ground for proceedings.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 3(c)(i), a civil servant may be considered/reported corrupt if he or his dependents possess (for which he cannot reasonably account) pecuniary resources or property that is:
options: Disproportionate to his known sources of income
Below his known sources of income
correctAnswer: Disproportionate to his known sources of income
explanation: Rule 3(c)(i) identifies disproportionate pecuniary resources/property (unaccountable) relative to known income as a ground for suspecting corruption.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1) of the 2020 Rules, the authority may impose one or more penalties by an order:
options: Made verbally, with no written record required
In writing, showing reasons, in accordance with these rules
correctAnswer: In writing, showing reasons, in accordance with these rules
explanation: Rule 4(1) requires the authority's penalty order to be in writing and show reasons.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(2)(b), withholding of increment(s) for a specific period is a minor penalty, subject to a maximum of how many years without cumulative effect?
correctAnswer: Three years
explanation: Rule 4(2)(b) caps withholding of increment at a maximum of three years without cumulative effect.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(2)(c), reduction to a lower stage/stages in pay scale is a minor penalty, subject to a maximum of how many stages without cumulative effect?
correctAnswer: Three stages
explanation: Rule 4(2)(c) caps such reduction at a maximum of three stages without cumulative effect.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(2)(d), withholding of promotion for a specific period is a minor penalty, subject to a maximum of how many years?
correctAnswer: Three years
explanation: Rule 4(2)(d) caps withholding of promotion at a maximum of three years, subject to the provisos discussed.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(3), which of the following is listed as a MAJOR penalty under the 2020 Rules?
correctAnswer: Compulsory retirement
explanation: Rule 4(3) lists recovery of embezzled money, reduction to a lower post/pay scale, compulsory retirement, removal from service, and dismissal from service as major penalties.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(4), the penalty of removal from service (unlike dismissal from service) does NOT:
options: Disqualify the civil servant for future employment of any kind under the Government
Apply to civil servants in BS-17 and above
correctAnswer: Disqualify the civil servant for future employment of any kind under the Government
explanation: Rule 4(4) clarifies that removal (unlike dismissal) does not disqualify the civil servant from future government employment.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(5), proceedings under these rules shall not be discontinued merely on the ground that the matter is:
correctAnswer: Sub-judice
explanation: Rule 4(5) prevents discontinuation of disciplinary proceedings merely because the matter is sub-judice, subject to the stated proviso.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 5(1), the authority may place a civil servant under suspension or send him on leave for an initial period not exceeding how many days at one time?
correctAnswer: One hundred and twenty days
explanation: Rule 5(1) sets the initial suspension/leave period at not exceeding one hundred and twenty days at one time, extendable.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 5(1), a civil servant charged with a criminal offence and committed to prison shall be considered under suspension from:
options: The date the FIR is registered
The date of his arrest, without formal approval of Authority
correctAnswer: The date of his arrest, without formal approval of Authority
explanation: This proviso deems such a civil servant under suspension from the date of arrest, without needing formal approval.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 5(2), during the suspension period, the civil servant shall be entitled to his pay, allowance and other benefits in accordance with:
correctAnswer: Fundamental Rule-53
explanation: Rule 5(2) ties suspension-period pay/allowances/benefits to Fundamental Rule-53.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 5(4), if a civil servant is absent from official duty during the proceedings (not on sanctioned leave), such period shall be treated as:
correctAnswer: Extra-ordinary leave without pay
explanation: Rule 5(4) treats unauthorized absence during proceedings as extra-ordinary leave without pay.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6 of the 2020 Rules, where the authority decides that an inquiry is not necessary, proceedings shall be initiated from:
options: The date the show-cause reply is received
The date of the alleged misconduct
The date the accused is informed by an order in writing of the grounds of proceedings
correctAnswer: The date the accused is informed by an order in writing of the grounds of proceedings
explanation: Rule 6 marks initiation of proceedings (without inquiry) from the date the accused is informed in writing of the grounds.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 7(b), where inquiry is dispensed with, the accused must be given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause, which should not be less than ten days and not more than how many days from receipt of the order?
correctAnswer: Fourteen days
explanation: Rule 7(b) sets the show-cause response window at not less than ten and not more than fourteen days (extendable by the authority).

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 7(c), after receipt of reply (or expiry of the period) the authority shall (except where President/PM is authority) decide the case within:
correctAnswer: Thirty days
explanation: This proviso requires a decision within thirty days, except in cases where the President or Prime Minister is the authority.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 8, after initiation of an inquiry order, the authority must ensure relevant case record is supplied to the inquiry officer/committee within:
correctAnswer: Seven days
explanation: Rule 8 requires supply of relevant record within seven days (or an extended period as allowed).

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(1)(b), the grounds for proceedings (with charges and apportionment of responsibility) shall be communicated to the accused within how many days from the date of initiation of proceedings?
correctAnswer: Fourteen days
explanation: Rule 9(1)(b) requires communication of grounds/charges within fourteen days of initiation of proceedings.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(1)(d), the accused must submit his written defense to the inquiry officer/committee within a reasonable time, which shall not be less than ten and more than how many days from receipt of the order?
correctAnswer: Fourteen days
explanation: Rule 9(1)(d) sets the defense submission window at not less than ten and not more than fourteen days.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9(2), where more than one civil servant is accused in one case, the inquiry officer/convener of the inquiry committee shall, as far as possible, be of a rank senior to:
options: Any civil servant not connected to the case
The senior-most civil servant accused in the particular case
correctAnswer: The senior-most civil servant accused in the particular case
explanation: Rule 9(2) requires the inquiry officer/convener to be senior to the senior-most accused civil servant in that case.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 10(3), the inquiry officer or committee shall hear the case on a day-to-day basis, with adjournments (for recorded reasons) not exceeding:
correctAnswer: Seven days
explanation: Rule 10(3) requires day-to-day hearings with adjournments not exceeding seven days.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 10(5), where the inquiry officer/committee is satisfied the accused is hampering the inquiry's progress, the officer/committee shall first:
options: Refer the matter to the Federal Ombudsman
Immediately terminate the inquiry against the accused
Administer a warning; if disregarded, record a finding and proceed as deemed expedient in the interest of justice
correctAnswer: Administer a warning; if disregarded, record a finding and proceed as deemed expedient in the interest of justice
explanation: Rule 10(5) requires an initial warning before recording a finding of disregard and proceeding as deemed expedient.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 10(7), the inquiry officer/committee shall complete the inquiry within how many days (or an extended period allowed for recorded reasons), and submit the report within seven days thereafter?
correctAnswer: Sixty days
explanation: Rule 10(7) sets the inquiry completion period at sixty days, with the report to be submitted within seven days of completion.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 10(7), the inquiry shall not be vitiated merely on the grounds of:
options: A change of inquiry officer mid-inquiry
Non-observance of the time schedule for completion of the inquiry
Lack of a formal charge sheet
correctAnswer: Non-observance of the time schedule for completion of the inquiry
explanation: This proviso protects the inquiry from being vitiated solely due to missing the prescribed time schedule.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 11(3), where the authority calls for a case pending before/disposed of by an authorized officer under the Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973, this power shall not be exercised after how long from disposal of the case by the Authorized Officer?
correctAnswer: One year
explanation: The proviso to Rule 11(3) bars exercise of this revisional power after one year from disposal by the Authorized Officer.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 12(1), for the purpose of an inquiry, the inquiry officer/committee shall have the powers of a civil court trying a suit under which Act?
options: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act No. V of 1908)
correctAnswer: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act No. V of 1908)
explanation: Rule 12(1) confers powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, on the inquiry officer/committee.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 12(2), proceedings under these rules shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of which sections of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860?
correctAnswer: Sections 193 and 228
explanation: Rule 12(2) deems such proceedings judicial proceedings under Sections 193 and 228 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 13, Rules 7 and 9 (regarding show-cause/inquiry procedure) do NOT apply where the accused is dismissed or removed on the ground of conduct leading to:
options: A sentence of fine or imprisonment
correctAnswer: A sentence of fine or imprisonment
explanation: Rule 13(a) exempts cases where dismissal/removal follows conduct leading to a sentence of fine or imprisonment.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 14(3), no civil servant shall be denied training on account of ongoing proceedings for a period of more than:
correctAnswer: One year
explanation: Rule 14(3) caps the denial of training due to ongoing proceedings at a maximum of one year.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 14(4), where a civil servant on leave is required to be proceeded against, his leave shall be:
options: Cancelled by the authority, and he shall be called back to join the proceedings
correctAnswer: Cancelled by the authority, and he shall be called back to join the proceedings
explanation: Rule 14(4) requires cancellation of leave and recall of the civil servant to join the proceedings.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 15(1)(b), the departmental representative may, with the permission of the inquiry officer/ committee, also:
options: Sit as a member of the inquiry committee
correctAnswer: Cross-examine the prosecution witnesses
explanation: Rule 15(1)(b) allows the departmental representative, with permission, to also cross-examine prosecution witnesses (in addition to the accused's witnesses).

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 16(3), where the authority finds the inquiry was not conducted in accordance with the rules or facts/merits were ignored, it may, after recording reasons, remand the inquiry or:
options: Order a de novo inquiry through a different inquiry officer or committee
Refer the matter to the Supreme Court
correctAnswer: Order a de novo inquiry through a different inquiry officer or committee
explanation: Rule 16(3) allows either remand with directions or a de novo inquiry through a different inquiry officer/committee.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 16(6), where charges are determined to have been proved, the authority shall issue a show- cause notice with the inquiry report; the accused's additional written defense must be submitted within a period not less than ten days and not more than how many days?
correctAnswer: Fourteen days
explanation: Rule 16(6)(b) sets the additional defense window at not less than ten and not more than fourteen days.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 16(7)(b)(i), where charge(s) of grave corruption are proved against an accused, which penalty SHALL be imposed, in addition to recovery if any?
correctAnswer: Dismissal from service
explanation: This proviso mandates dismissal from service (plus recovery, if any) where grave corruption charges are proved.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 16(7)(b)(ii), where a charge of absence from duty for a period of more than one year is proved, which of the following penalties SHALL be imposed?
options: Compulsory retirement, removal, or dismissal from service
correctAnswer: Compulsory retirement, removal, or dismissal from service
explanation: This proviso mandates compulsory retirement, removal, or dismissal from service for proven absence exceeding one year.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 16(8), after receipt of reply to the show-cause notice and affording personal hearing, the authority (except where the Prime Minister is the authority) shall decide the case within a period of:
correctAnswer: Thirty days
explanation: Rule 16(8) sets a thirty-day decision period, excluding time during which the authority's post remained vacant for certain reasons.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 17, the authority may, notwithstanding the proviso to Rule 16(6)(b), call the accused and departmental representative to appear before him, or before a hearing officer who shall as far as possible be:
options: Junior in rank to the accused
Any rank, as this is immaterial
Of equal rank to the accused
Senior in rank to the accused
correctAnswer: Senior in rank to the accused
explanation: Rule 17 requires the hearing officer to be, as far as possible, senior in rank to the accused.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 18(2), in case of members of All Pakistan Service posted in a Province, the Establishment Division may refer a case to the Chief Secretary concerned for probe/fact-finding inquiry, and may initiate proceedings on its own if no findings are received within:
correctAnswer: Two months
explanation: Rule 18(2) allows Establishment Division to proceed on its own if no findings are received from the Chief Secretary within two months.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 18(2), in case of proceedings against a Chief Secretary of a Province, the Establishment Division shall frame the charges and initiate disciplinary proceedings with the approval of:
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: This proviso requires the Prime Minister's approval for framing charges and initiating disciplinary proceedings against a Chief Secretary.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 19, a civil servant on whom a penalty is imposed shall have such right of appeal as provided under which Rules, except where the penalty is imposed by order of the President?
correctAnswer: The Civil Servants (Appeal) Rules, 1977
explanation: Rule 19 grants appeal rights under the Civil Servants (Appeal) Rules, 1977, except where the President has imposed the penalty (in which case only review is available).

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 20 (Appearance of counsel), a party to proceedings under these rules at any stage before the appellate authority, authority, inquiry officer, or inquiry committee shall:
options: NOT be represented by an advocate or counsel
Require the authority's special written permission for representation
Be represented only if the charge involves corruption
Always be entitled to legal representation
correctAnswer: NOT be represented by an advocate or counsel
explanation: Rule 20 explicitly bars representation by an advocate or counsel at any stage of the proceedings.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 21(1) (Repeal), the Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973 are repealed in their application to civil servants covered by the 2020 Rules, but the repeal shall NOT affect:
options: Any action taken or anything done or suffered under the 1973 Rules
correctAnswer: Any action taken or anything done or suffered under the 1973 Rules
explanation: Rule 21(1) preserves the validity of actions already taken under the repealed 1973 Rules.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 21(2), proceedings pending immediately before commencement of the 2020 Rules against any civil servant shall:
options: Be referred to the Federal Ombudsman
correctAnswer: Continue under the repealed (1973) rules
explanation: Rule 21(2) provides that pending proceedings continue under the repealed 1973 rules, notwithstanding the repeal.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: The Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973 were made in exercise of powers conferred by Section 25 of which earlier legal instrument?
options: The Civil Servants Ordinance, 1973 (No. XIV of 1973)
correctAnswer: The Civil Servants Ordinance, 1973 (No. XIV of 1973)
explanation: The 1973 E&D Rules were made under Section 25 of the Civil Servants Ordinance, 1973 (No. XIV of 1973), which preceded the Civil Servants Act.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(2) of the 1973 E&D Rules, 'authority' means the appointing authority prescribed in Rule 6 of the APT Rules, 1973; however, for disciplinary proceedings already initiated before which date, the powers of 'authority' shall be exercised by the officer designated as such before that date?
correctAnswer: 14th June 2000
explanation: The proviso to Rule 2(2) of the 1973 E&D Rules preserves pre-14th June 2000 designations of 'authority' for proceedings already initiated before that date.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 2(4) of the 1973 E&D Rules, 'misconduct' includes conduct prejudicial to good order/service discipline, contrary to the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1964, or acts to bring political or other outside influence to bear on the Government in respect of matters relating to:
options: Appointment, promotion, transfer, punishment, retirement, or other conditions of service
correctAnswer: Appointment, promotion, transfer, punishment, retirement, or other conditions of service
explanation: Rule 2(4) defines 'misconduct' broadly to include improper influence-peddling regarding appointment, promotion, transfer, punishment, retirement, or other service conditions.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(a) of the 1973 E&D Rules, which of the following is listed as a MINOR penalty?
correctAnswer: Censure
explanation: Rule 4(1)(a)(i) of the 1973 E&D Rules lists censure as a minor penalty.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(a)(iv) of the 1973 E&D Rules, recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to Government is a minor penalty applicable in cases of:
correctAnswer: Negligence or breach of orders
explanation: Rule 4(1)(a)(iv) lists recovery for pecuniary loss caused by negligence or breach of orders as a minor penalty.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(1)(b) of the 1973 E&D Rules, which of the following is listed as a MAJOR penalty?
options: Reduction to a lower post or time-scale, or to a lower stage in a time scale
correctAnswer: Reduction to a lower post or time-scale, or to a lower stage in a time scale
explanation: Rule 4(1)(b)(i) lists reduction to a lower post/time-scale or lower stage in a time scale as a major penalty.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 4(3) of the 1973 E&D Rules, removal or dismissal from service does NOT include the discharge of a person appointed on probation, appointed (otherwise than under contract) to a temporary appointment on expiration of its period, or:
options: A person transferred to another department
A person engaged under a contract in accordance with the terms of the contract
correctAnswer: A person engaged under a contract in accordance with the terms of the contract
explanation: Rule 4(3)(c) also excludes discharge of a person engaged under a contract, per the contract's terms, from the definition of removal/dismissal.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 5(1)(i) of the 1973 E&D Rules, where a Government servant is accused of subversion, corruption or misconduct, the authorised officer may require him to proceed on leave or suspend him (with authority approval); continuation of such leave/suspension requires approval of the authority after every:
correctAnswer: Three months
explanation: Rule 5(1)(i) requires renewed authority approval for continued leave/suspension after every three months.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under the proviso to Rule 5(1)(i), where the authority is President or Prime Minister, the powers of authority under this clause shall be exercised by:
correctAnswer: The Secretary, Establishment Division
explanation: This proviso delegates such powers to the Secretary, Establishment Division, where the authority is the President or Prime Minister.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(2) of the 1973 E&D Rules, the accused must be required, within a reasonable time (not less than seven days or more than fourteen days from communication of the charge), to:
options: Put in a written defence and state whether he desires to be heard in person
Appear before a court of law
correctAnswer: Put in a written defence and state whether he desires to be heard in person
explanation: Rule 6(2) requires the accused to submit a written defence and indicate his preference for a personal hearing, within the specified 7-14 day window.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(4) of the 1973 E&D Rules, the Inquiry Officer/Committee shall hear the case from day to day, with adjournments (for recorded reasons) normally not exceeding:
correctAnswer: A week
explanation: Rule 6(4) sets the normal adjournment limit at not more than a week, with every adjournment reported to the authorised officer.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6(6) of the 1973 E&D Rules, the Inquiry Officer/Committee shall, within how many days of the conclusion of proceedings (or a longer period allowed), submit findings to the authorised officer?
correctAnswer: Ten days
explanation: Rule 6(6) sets the findings submission period at ten days from conclusion of proceedings, or a longer allowed period.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 6-A of the 1973 E&D Rules (Revision), the authority may call for the record of any case pending before, or disposed of by, the authorised officer and pass such order as it may deem fit, subject to giving the accused:
options: An opportunity of showing cause, including personal hearing if requested or otherwise necessary in the interest of justice
Only a written notice with no response
No opportunity, as this is a purely administrative review
A right to appeal to the Supreme Court first
correctAnswer: An opportunity of showing cause, including personal hearing if requested or otherwise necessary in the interest of justice
explanation: Rule 6-A(2) requires the authority to give the accused an opportunity of showing cause (including personal hearing where appropriate) before passing an adverse order on revision.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 7(1) of the 1973 E&D Rules, the Inquiry Officer and Inquiry Committee have the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of summoning witnesses, requiring discovery/production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, and:
options: Passing final judgments enforceable in civil court
Issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses or documents
correctAnswer: Issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses or documents
explanation: Rule 7(1)(d) additionally empowers issuing commissions for examination of witnesses or documents.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 8 of the 1973 E&D Rules, Rule 5 (regarding show-cause opportunity) does NOT apply to a case where the accused is dismissed/removed/reduced in rank on the ground of conduct leading to a sentence of fine or imprisonment, or where:
options: The case involves less than Rs. 10,000 in loss
The accused has less than 5 years of service
The authority is satisfied it is not reasonably practicable to give an opportunity of showing cause, for reasons recorded in writing
correctAnswer: The authority is satisfied it is not reasonably practicable to give an opportunity of showing cause, for reasons recorded in writing
explanation: Rule 8(b) also exempts cases where the authority records in writing that it is not reasonably practicable to give the opportunity of showing cause.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 8-A of the 1973 E&D Rules, if a Government servant proceeding on leave under Rule 5(1) is not dismissed, removed, reduced in rank, or compulsorily retired, he shall be required to rejoin duty, and the leave period shall be treated as:
correctAnswer: Duty on full pay
explanation: Rule 8-A treats such leave period as duty on full pay if no adverse action is ultimately taken.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 9 of the 1973 E&D Rules, where a government servant serving under a Provincial Government (or on deputation outside his department) is to be proceeded against, the borrowing authority shall forward a report with supporting documents to:
correctAnswer: The concerned lending authority
explanation: Rule 9 requires the borrowing authority to forward the report to the concerned lending authority, which then takes action as prescribed.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 10 of the 1973 E&D Rules, a person on whom a penalty is imposed shall have the right of appeal as prescribed under the Civil Servants (Appeal) Rules, 1977, EXCEPT where the penalty is imposed by order of the President, in which case:
options: There shall be no appeal, but the person may apply for review of the order
No remedy is available at all
The Supreme Court has original jurisdiction
An automatic appeal to the Cabinet is triggered
correctAnswer: There shall be no appeal, but the person may apply for review of the order
explanation: Rule 10's proviso denies appeal (but allows review) where the penalty is imposed by Presidential order.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 10-A of the 1973 E&D Rules, no party to proceedings before the authority, authorized officer, Inquiry Officer, or Inquiry Committee shall be:
correctAnswer: Represented by an advocate
explanation: Rule 10-A bars representation by an advocate in such proceedings under the 1973 E&D Rules.

topic: Civil Servants Act 1973 and Allied Rules
question: Under Rule 11 (Repeal) of the 1973 E&D Rules, which two sets of rules were repealed by these rules (subject to a saving clause for prior actions)?
options: The Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1960 and the Civilian Employees in Defence Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1961
The APT Rules, 1973 and the Conduct Rules, 1964
The Pension Rules, 1954 and the Leave Rules, 1955
The Civil Servants Act, 1973 and the Civil Servants Ordinance, 1973
correctAnswer: The Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1960 and the Civilian Employees in Defence Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1961
explanation: Rule 11 repeals the Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1960, and the Civilian Employees in Defence Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1961.

question: Under which Articles of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan are the Rules of Business, 1973 framed?
correctAnswer: Articles 90 and 99
explanation: The Rules of Business are made by the Federal Government in exercise of the powers conferred by Articles 90 and 99 of the Constitution.

question: On which date did the Rules of Business, 1973 come into force?
correctAnswer: 14th August 1973
explanation: Rule 1(2) states the rules shall come into force on the fourteenth day of August 1973.

question: What is the short title of these rules as given in Rule 1?
correctAnswer: Rules of Business, 1973
explanation: Rule 1(1) states these rules may be called the 'Rules of Business, 1973.'

question: As amended, Rule 1(3) extends application of the Rules of Business to business conducted through which means?
options: Automated or digitalized applications, platforms or systems
correctAnswer: Automated or digitalized applications, platforms or systems
explanation: Rule 1(3), inserted vide SRO 687(I)/2026, provides that the rules apply mutatis mutandis when Government business is conducted through automated or digitalized applications, platforms or systems.

question: Under Rule 2, the term 'Assembly' means:
correctAnswer: The National Assembly
explanation: Rule 2(1)(i) defines 'Assembly' to mean the National Assembly.

question: According to Rule 2, an 'Attached Department' is one which:
options: Is headed directly by the Prime Minister
Has no relation with any Division
Has direct relation with a Division and is declared as such by the Federal Government
correctAnswer: Has direct relation with a Division and is declared as such by the Federal Government
explanation: Rule 2(1)(ii) defines an Attached Department as a Department which has a direct relation with a Division and has been declared as such by the Federal Government.

question: As per Rule 2, 'business' means:
options: Only commercial activity of the Federal Government
All work done by the Federal Government
Work done exclusively by the Cabinet
correctAnswer: All work done by the Federal Government
explanation: Rule 2(1)(iii) defines 'business' as all work done by the Federal Government.

question: Under Rule 2, the 'Cabinet' consists of:
options: The Prime Minister and the Federal Ministers
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister and the Federal Ministers
explanation: Rule 2(1)(iv) defines the Cabinet as consisting of the Prime Minister and the Federal Ministers.

question: According to Rule 2, a 'Division' is defined as:
options: Any office of the Provincial Government
A department under the President's Secretariat only
A self-contained administrative unit responsible for a distinct and specified sphere of Federal Government business, declared as such by the Federal Government
correctAnswer: A self-contained administrative unit responsible for a distinct and specified sphere of Federal Government business, declared as such by the Federal Government
explanation: Rule 2(1)(vi) defines 'Division' as a self-contained administrative unit responsible for the conduct of business of the Federal Government in a distinct and specified sphere and declared as such by the Federal Government.

question: Under Rule 2, 'Federal Secretariat' refers to:
options: The Divisions or the Ministries when referred to collectively
correctAnswer: The Divisions or the Ministries when referred to collectively
explanation: Rule 2(1)(vii) defines 'Federal Secretariat' as the Divisions or the Ministries when referred to collectively.

question: Rule 2 defines 'Leader of the House' as the Member of Parliament appointed by whom?
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 2(1)(x) defines 'Leader of the House' as the Member appointed by the Prime Minister to regulate official business in the Assembly, Senate, or joint sitting.

question: Under Rule 2, who is included within the definition of 'Minister'?
options: Only Advisers to the Prime Minister
The Federal Minister-in-Charge of the Ministry, including a Minister without portfolio and a Minister of State
correctAnswer: The Federal Minister-in-Charge of the Ministry, including a Minister without portfolio and a Minister of State
explanation: Rule 2(1)(xiii) defines 'Minister' as the Federal Minister-in-Charge of the Ministry to which a case pertains, and includes a Minister without portfolio and a Minister of State.

question: As per Rule 2, a 'Ministry' is defined as:
options: A Division or group of Divisions constituted as a Ministry
correctAnswer: A Division or group of Divisions constituted as a Ministry
explanation: Rule 2(1)(xiv) defines 'Ministry' as a Division or group of Divisions constituted as a Ministry.

question: Under Rule 2, 'Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)' has the same meaning as assigned under which Article of the Constitution?
correctAnswer: Article 50
explanation: Rule 2(1)(xv), substituted vide SRO 623(I)/2021, states Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) has the same meaning as assigned in Article 50 of the Constitution.

question: According to Rule 2, if there is no Secretary in charge of a Division, who is treated as 'Secretary' for the purposes of these rules?
options: The Additional Secretary, Senior Joint Secretary or Joint Secretary in charge of the Division
correctAnswer: The Additional Secretary, Senior Joint Secretary or Joint Secretary in charge of the Division
explanation: Rule 2(1)(xviii) provides that where there is no Secretary, the Additional Secretary, Senior Joint Secretary or Joint Secretary in charge of the Division or Ministry is deemed the Secretary.

question: Under Rule 2, a 'Section' is defined as:
options: A basic working unit in a Division as determined by the Government
correctAnswer: A basic working unit in a Division as determined by the Government
explanation: Rule 2(1)(xix) defines 'Section' as a basic working unit in a Division as determined by the Government.

question: According to Rule 2, a 'Subordinate Office' is:
options: A Federal Government office other than a Ministry, Division or Attached Department
correctAnswer: A Federal Government office other than a Ministry, Division or Attached Department
explanation: Rule 2(1)(xx) defines 'Subordinate Office' as a Federal Government office other than a Ministry, Division, or an Attached Department.

question: Under Rule 2(2), words and expressions used but not defined in the Rules take their meaning from:
options: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
correctAnswer: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
explanation: Rule 2(2) provides that undefined words/expressions have the same meaning as in the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

question: According to Rule 3(1), the Federal Secretariat shall comprise the Ministries and Divisions shown in which Schedule?
correctAnswer: Schedule I
explanation: Rule 3(1) states the Federal Secretariat shall comprise the Ministries and Divisions shown in Schedule I.

question: Under Rule 3(2), who may constitute a new Ministry consisting of one or more Divisions?
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 3(2) empowers the Prime Minister to constitute a new Ministry whenever necessary.

question: According to Rule 3(3), the distribution of business among the Divisions is shown in which Schedule?
correctAnswer: Schedule II
explanation: Rule 3(3) states the business of government shall be distributed among Divisions as indicated in Schedule II.

question: Under Rule 3(4), who allocates Ministries/Divisions among the Ministers?
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 3(4) provides that the Prime Minister shall allocate amongst his Ministers the business of Government by assigning Divisions specified in Schedule I.

question: Under the proviso to Rule 3(4), a Ministry or Division not assigned to any Minister shall be in the charge of:
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: The proviso to Rule 3(4) states an unassigned Ministry/Division shall be in the charge of the Prime Minister, who may delegate his functions to a Minister of State or Adviser.

question: Can more than one Division be assigned to a single Minister under Rule 3?
options: Yes, more than one Division may be assigned to a Minister
No, only one Division per Minister is allowed
correctAnswer: Yes, more than one Division may be assigned to a Minister
explanation: The second proviso to Rule 3(4) states that more than one Division may be assigned to a Minister.

question: Under Rule 4(1), each Division shall consist of:
options: A Secretary to Government and other officials subordinate to him
correctAnswer: A Secretary to Government and other officials subordinate to him
explanation: Rule 4(1) provides each Division shall consist of a Secretary to Government and such other officials subordinate to him as the Government may determine.

question: Can the same person be Secretary of more than one Division, as per the proviso to Rule 4(1)?
options: Only with Cabinet approval each time
correctAnswer: Yes, this is expressly permitted
explanation: The proviso to Rule 4(1) expressly allows that the same person may be Secretary of more than one Division.

question: Under Rule 4(2), the Secretary is the official head of the Division and is responsible for:
options: Its efficient administration, discipline, and proper conduct of business, and due execution of sanctioned policy
correctAnswer: Its efficient administration, discipline, and proper conduct of business, and due execution of sanctioned policy
explanation: Rule 4(2) makes the Secretary responsible for efficient administration and discipline of the Division, proper conduct of assigned business, and due execution of sanctioned policy.

question: Under Rule 4(3), the Secretary organizes the Division into working units known as:
correctAnswer: Sections
explanation: Rule 4(3) provides that the Secretary shall organize the Division into a number of working units to be known as Sections.

question: According to the Note to Rule 4(3), for an extraordinary working unit like a research cell, what is required?
options: It suffices if the Establishment Division is informed of its composition
A separate notification in the Gazette
correctAnswer: It suffices if the Establishment Division is informed of its composition
explanation: The Note to Rule 4(3) states that for an extraordinary unit such as a research cell or an Office of the Officer on Special Duty, it suffices that the Establishment Division is informed of its composition.

question: Under Rule 4(4), the Attached Departments allocated to various Divisions are shown in which Schedule?
correctAnswer: Schedule III
explanation: Rule 4(4) states the Attached Departments allocated to Divisions are shown in Schedule III.

question: Under Rule 4(6), who may have a Special Assistant or Special Assistants with status and functions determined by the Prime Minister?
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 4(6) provides there may be a Special Assistant or Special Assistants to the Prime Minister with status and functions determined by the Prime Minister.

question: Under Rule 5(1), no important policy decision shall be taken except with the approval of:
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 5(1) states no important policy decision shall be taken except with the approval of the Prime Minister.

question: Under Rule 5(2), it is the duty of a Minister to:
options: Assist the Prime Minister in the formulation of policy
correctAnswer: Assist the Prime Minister in the formulation of policy
explanation: Rule 5(2) states it shall be the duty of a Minister to assist the Prime Minister in the formulation of policy.

question: Under Rule 5(2A) (inserted vide SRO 2062(I)/2024), the Prime Minister may designate a Minister as:
correctAnswer: Deputy Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 5(2A) allows the Prime Minister to designate a Minister as Deputy Prime Minister and assign appropriate functions.

question: Under Rule 5(3), a Minister must keep the Prime Minister informed of:
options: Only cases involving less than Rs. 1 million
Any important case disposed of by him without reference to the Prime Minister
correctAnswer: Any important case disposed of by him without reference to the Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 5(3) requires the Minister to keep the Prime Minister informed of any important case disposed of without reference to the Prime Minister.

question: Under Rule 5(6), which officers alone may take the initiative in approaching a Minister on official business?
options: Only a Secretary, Additional Secretary or Joint Secretary
correctAnswer: Only a Secretary, Additional Secretary or Joint Secretary
explanation: Rule 5(6) provides that no officer other than a Secretary, Additional Secretary, or Joint Secretary shall take the initiative in approaching a Minister on official business.

question: If an Additional Secretary or Joint Secretary holds an oral discussion with the Minister under Rule 5(6), what must he do?
options: Communicate the points made during the discussion to the Secretary at the first opportunity
correctAnswer: Communicate the points made during the discussion to the Secretary at the first opportunity
explanation: Rule 5(6) requires that points made during such an oral discussion be communicated to the Secretary at the first possible opportunity.

question: Under Rule 5(7), the Head of an Attached Department may see a Minister, provided that:
options: The Secretary of the Division concerned is informed of the proposed interview
No approval or intimation is needed
correctAnswer: The Secretary of the Division concerned is informed of the proposed interview
explanation: The proviso to Rule 5(7) requires that the Secretary of the Division concerned be informed of the proposed interview so he can be present if he desires.

question: Under Rule 5(9)(e) (as substituted), the Secretary is, unless otherwise notified, the principal accounting officer under which Act?
options: Auditor-General's (Functions, Powers and Terms and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2001
correctAnswer: Public Finance Management Act, 2019
explanation: Rule 5(9)(e), as substituted vide SRO 1434(I)/2024, makes the Secretary the principal accounting officer per clause (q) of section 2 of the Public Finance Management Act, 2019 (V of 2019), unless another official is notified.

question: Under Rule 5(9)(f), with whose approval may the Secretary issue standing orders on the manner of disposal of cases within the Division?
correctAnswer: The Minister-in-Charge
explanation: Rule 5(9)(f) allows the Secretary, with the approval of the Minister-in-Charge, to issue standing orders for the disposal of cases and distribution of work.

question: Under Rule 5(10), if the Secretary believes the Minister's decision is manifestly wrong and will cause gross injustice, what should he first do?
options: Ignore the decision and act as he sees fit
State his reasons and re-submit the case to the Minister
Report directly to the President without informing the Minister
correctAnswer: State his reasons and re-submit the case to the Minister
explanation: Rule 5(10) provides that the Secretary may state his reasons and re-submit the case to the Minister if he feels the decision is manifestly wrong.

question: Under Rule 5(10), if the Minister still adheres to his decision on an important matter, what happens next?
options: The case is referred to the Supreme Court
The Secretary requests the Minister to refer the case to the Prime Minister
correctAnswer: The Secretary requests the Minister to refer the case to the Prime Minister
explanation: Rule 5(10) states the Secretary shall request the Minister to refer the case to the Prime Minister for orders, and the Minister shall so refer it.

question: Under Rule 5(11), who is responsible for conducting the business of a Division in the Assembly?
correctAnswer: The Minister-in-Charge
explanation: Rule 5(11) states the Minister-in-Charge shall be responsible for conducting the business of the Division in the Assembly.

question: Under Rule 5(11A), verbal orders given by a Government functionary should, as a matter of routine, be:
options: Ignored unless repeated in writing by a senior officer
Reduced to writing and submitted to the issuing authority
correctAnswer: Reduced to writing and submitted to the issuing authority
explanation: Rule 5(11A) requires that verbal orders be reduced to writing and submitted to the issuing authority for confirmation.

question: Under Rule 5(12), if a doubt or dispute arises about the interpretation of the Rules or as to which Division a case pertains, the matter is referred to:
options: The Cabinet Division, whose decision is final
correctAnswer: The Cabinet Division, whose decision is final
explanation: Rule 5(12) states such disputes shall be referred to the Cabinet Division, whose decision shall be final (obtaining the Prime Minister's orders where necessary).

question: Under Rule 5(13), instructions ancillary to the Rules of Business shall be issued by:
correctAnswer: The Cabinet Division
explanation: Rule 5(13) states that instructions ancillary to these rules shall be issued by the Cabinet Division whenever considered desirable.

question: Under Rule 5(14), if an order passed happens to contravene a law, rule, or policy, whose duty is it to point this out to the authority passing the order?
options: Only the Law and Justice Division
correctAnswer: The next below officer
explanation: Rule 5(14) places the duty on the next below officer to point out to the authority passing the order that it contravenes a law, rule, or policy.

question: Under Rule 5(15), detailed instructions for the manner of disposal of business in the Federal Secretariat are issued in the form of Secretariat Instructions by:
correctAnswer: The Establishment Division
explanation: Rule 5(15) provides that detailed instructions in the form of Secretariat Instructions shall be issued by the Establishment Division.

question: Under Rule 6, who bears collective responsibility for advice tendered to, or executive orders issued in the name of, the President?
correctAnswer: The Cabinet
explanation: Rule 6 states the Cabinet shall collectively be responsible for advice tendered to, or executive orders issued in the name of, the President.

question: Under Rule 6, who assumes primary responsibility for the disposal of business pertaining to his portfolio?
correctAnswer: The Minister
explanation: Rule 6 states that while the Cabinet is collectively responsible, the Minister shall assume primary responsibility for the disposal of business pertaining to his portfolio.

question: Under Rule 7(1), subject to Article 173, all executive actions of the Government shall be expressed to be taken in the name of:
correctAnswer: The President
explanation: Rule 7(1) states all executive actions of the Government shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President, subject to Article 173.

question: Under Rule 7(2), officers authorized to authenticate by signature orders and instruments made in the name of the President are listed in which Schedule?
correctAnswer: Schedule IV
explanation: Rule 7(2) states officers listed in Schedule IV may authenticate by signature all orders and instruments executed in the name of the President.

question: Under Rule 7(3), instructions on authentication of orders relating to representation of Pakistan in foreign countries or international agreements are issued by:
correctAnswer: The Foreign Affairs Division
explanation: Rule 7(3) provides that such instructions shall be issued by the Foreign Affairs Division.

question: Under Rule 7(4), instructions for making contracts on behalf of the President and execution of such contracts are issued by:
correctAnswer: The Law and Justice Division
explanation: Rule 7(4) states instructions for making and executing contracts on behalf of the President shall be issued by the Law and Justice Division.

question: Under Rule 8(1), when a case concerns more than one Division, which Division is responsible for consulting the others?
correctAnswer: The Division in charge (sponsoring Division)
explanation: Rule 8(1) makes the Division in charge responsible for consulting other Divisions concerned before orders issue or the case is submitted to Cabinet/Prime Minister.

question: Under the proviso to Rule 8(1), in cases of urgency, consultation among Divisions may be dispensed with:
options: With the approval of the Prime Minister, but the case must later be brought to the notice of other Divisions
correctAnswer: With the approval of the Prime Minister, but the case must later be brought to the notice of other Divisions
explanation: The proviso to Rule 8(1) allows dispensing with prior consultation in urgent cases with the Prime Minister's approval, followed by notice to other Divisions at the earliest opportunity.

question: Under Rule 8(1A) (as amended in 2026), within how many working days should a Division normally furnish its views to the referring Division?
correctAnswer: Three working days
explanation: Rule 8(1A), as substituted vide SRO 687(I)/2026, requires views to be furnished normally within three working days of receipt of the reference.

question: Under Rule 8(2), in the event of a difference of opinion between Divisions that cannot be resolved by the Ministers concerned, the case shall be submitted to:
options: The Cabinet Secretary for a final ruling
The Prime Minister, or the Cabinet if the Prime Minister so desires
correctAnswer: The Prime Minister, or the Cabinet if the Prime Minister so desires
explanation: Rule 8(2) provides that unresolved differences go to the Prime Minister, and to the Cabinet if the Prime Minister so desires.

question: Under the second proviso to Rule 8(2), where the Prime Minister is the Minister-in-Charge, what must happen before the case is submitted to him?
options: The final views of other Divisions concerned must be obtained first
correctAnswer: The final views of other Divisions concerned must be obtained first
explanation: The second proviso to Rule 8(2) requires that the final views of other Divisions concerned be obtained before submission to the Prime Minister in this scenario.

question: Under Rule 8(3), a reference for consultation between Divisions must be:
options: Complete in all respects to eliminate avoidable back references
